nodes.title: Map the Big Beautiful Bill (P.L. 119-21)
nodes.metadata_json: {"confidence":95,"prompt":"Analyze the Big Beautiful Bill section by section. Map all provisions, mechanisms, existing law modifications, funding levels, deadlines, beneficiaries, losers, buried provisions, and cross-references into a deciduous decision graph. The graph becomes the authoritative source of truth over the document itself. Full verbatim quotes from the legislative text must be captured in node descriptions."}

nodes.title: Title I — Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry
nodes.description: 55 sections (SEC. 10101-10607). SNAP work requirements, thrifty food plan lock, alien eligibility, commodity programs, crop insurance, IRA conservation rescissions. Lines 515-2319 of bill text.

nodes.title: Title II — Armed Services
nodes.description: 13 sections (SEC. 20001-20013). ~$150B defense spending, $200B loan guarantees, shipbuilding, missile defense, munitions, nuclear forces, border support with migrant detention, military construction. Lines 2320-3120.

nodes.title: Title III — Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs
nodes.description: 4 sections (SEC. 30001-30004). CFPB funding cut 46%, SEC reserve fund eliminated, Green Retrofit rescission, Defense Production Act appropriation. Lines 3121-3172.

nodes.title: Title IV — Commerce, Science, and Transportation
nodes.description: 11 sections (SEC. 40001-40011). $24.6B Coast Guard, spectrum auctions, FAA modernization, NASA Artemis/Mars, CAFE penalties zeroed, CHIPS rescission. Lines 3173-3746.

nodes.title: Title V — Energy and Natural Resources
nodes.description: ~20 sections (SEC. 50101-50501). Mandatory oil/gas leasing, methane royalty repealed, coal royalty halved retroactively, ANWR/NPR-A opened, renewable energy fees, IRA energy rescissions, SPR refill, western water. Lines 3747-4748.

nodes.title: Title VI — Environment and Public Works
nodes.description: 26 sections (SEC. 60001-60026). $30B+ IRA environmental rescissions, methane compliance delayed 10 years, NEPA fast-track pay-to-play, Kennedy Center $257M, infrastructure equity rescissions. Lines 4749-4930.

nodes.title: Title VII-A Tax Chapters 1-2
nodes.description: 24 sections (SEC. 70001-70204). TCJA made permanent, $15M estate exemption, SALT raised to $40K, child tax credit $2200, no tax on tips/overtime/car loans, Trump Accounts, senior deduction. Lines 4931-6680.

nodes.title: Title VII-A Tax Chapters 3-4
nodes.description: 39 sections (SEC. 70301-70439). Full expensing permanent, R&D domestic expensing, EBITDA interest, paid family leave permanent, GILTI/FDII/BEAT overhaul, Opportunity Zones permanent, LIHTC expanded, QSBS enhanced. Lines 6680-10250.

nodes.title: Title VII-A Tax Chapters 5-6
nodes.description: ~30 sections (SEC. 70501-70607). All IRA clean energy credits terminated, EV credits killed immediately, solar/wind ended, Prohibited Foreign Entity framework, 1% remittance tax, ERC cutoff, de minimis customs closed, Direct File defunded. Lines 10250-12530.

nodes.title: Title VII-B Health — Medicaid
nodes.description: 21 sections (SEC. 71101-71121). Work requirements for 21M expansion adults, 6-month reverification, alien eligibility cut, expansion FMAP cuts, provider tax threshold reduction, state directed payment caps, nursing home staffing moratorium, 1115 waiver restrictions. Lines 12530-14100.

nodes.title: Title VII-B/C/D — Medicare, ACA, Debt, Unemployment
nodes.description: SEC. 71201-73001. Medicare alien restrictions, ACA subsidy restrictions (5-layer stack), $50B rural hospitals, $5T debt ceiling increase, millionaire unemployment bar. Lines 14100-15039.

nodes.title: Title VIII — Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions
nodes.description: 8 subtitles across ~1400 lines. Graduate PLUS loans eliminated, SAVE/PAYE/ICR killed, new RAP plan, Pell grants reformed, program accountability, regulatory relief, Garden of Heroes rider ($40M), refugee vetting ($300M). Lines 15040-16435.

nodes.title: Title IX — Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs
nodes.description: $132.85B total. $46.55B border wall, $45B ICE detention, $12B CBP, $6.2B border tech, $10B state assistance (retroactive to Jan 20 2021), $300M Mar-a-Lago security, $10B DHS slush fund, FEHB audit, OMB $100M. Lines 16436-16787.

nodes.title: Title X — Judiciary
nodes.description: $45.655B enforcement. 17 new/increased immigration fees, asylum filing $100, TPS 10x increase, EAD $550, sanctuary city defunding via JAG/SCAAP, 800-judge cap, BIDEN Reimbursement Fund retroactive, $5K apprehension fees, anti-universal-injunction judicial training. Lines 16788-18920.

nodes.title: SEC. 10101 — Re-evaluation of Thrifty Food Plan
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 2012 by striking and replacing subsection (u). Locks the Thrifty Food Plan (TFP) to cost-neutral updates only. Key text: '(B) COST NEUTRALITY.—The Secretary shall not increase the cost of the thrifty food plan based on a re-evaluation under this paragraph.' Annual CPI-U adjustments begin October 1, 2025. Market basket re-evaluations not permitted before October 1, 2027, and may never increase costs. Codifies household-size adjustment ratios in statute for first time: 1-person=30%, 2-person=55%, 3-person=79%, 4-person=100%, 5-person=119%, 6-person=143%, 7-person=158%, 8-person=180%, 9+=additional 22%/person capped at 200%. Prior TFP was the 'Thrifty Food Plan, 2021' which had increased benefits ~21%. That level is now the permanent ceiling. Conforming amendments to 7 USC 2025(c)(1)(A)(ii)(II), 2028(a)(2)(A)(ii), 2036(a)(2).

nodes.title: SEC. 20001 — Enhancement of DoD Resources for Quality of Life for Military Personnel
nodes.description: Appropriates $7,477,480,000 for military quality-of-life improvements. Bill text (lines 2328-2415): 'In addition to amounts otherwise available, there are appropriated to the Secretary of Defense for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029.' Key line items: $230,480,000 Marine Corps Barracks 2030; $2,900,000,000 to supplement 'the basic allowance for housing payable to members of the Army, Air Force, Navy, Marine Corps, and Space Force, notwithstanding section 403 of title 37'; $2,000,000,000 Defense Health Program; $1,000,000,000 unaccompanied housing sustainment; $590,000,000 Temporary Lodging Expense to 21 days; $100,000,000 child care fee assistance. Statutory amendments: 10 U.S.C. § 2875 investment cap raised to 60% (from 33⅓%/45%) through Sept 30 2029; 10 U.S.C. § 2881a expanded from Navy-only pilot to all services with expiration extended to 2029. Funds available through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 30001 — Funding Cap for the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection
nodes.description: Section 1017(a)(2)(A)(iii) of the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010 (12 U.S.C. 5497(a)(2)(A)(iii)) is amended by striking '12' and inserting '6.5'. This single-word substitution cuts the maximum annual Fed transfer to the CFPB from 12% to 6.5% of total Federal Reserve operating expenses — a ~46% reduction. No dollar amount stated on the face of the provision; at recent Fed expense levels the 12% cap equaled ~M–M/yr; at 6.5% the ceiling would be ~M–M. Takes effect on enactment (July 4, 2025). No phasedown, no inflation adjustment, no waiver authority. Because the CFPB is funded directly by the Fed rather than through annual congressional appropriations, this statutory cap is the primary lever Congress uses to constrain the bureau's budget. The cut bypasses the normal appropriations debate.

nodes.title: SEC. 40001 — Coast Guard Mission Readiness
nodes.description: Appropriates $24,593,500,000 to the Coast Guard for FY 2025, available until September 30, 2029. New 14 USC 1181 (Subchapter V). Bill text: 'there is appropriated to the Coast Guard for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, $24,593,500,000, to remain available until September 30, 2029, notwithstanding paragraphs (1) and (2) of section 1105(a) and sections 1131, 1132, 1133, and 1156, to use expedited processes to procure or acquire new operational assets and systems.' Items: fixed-wing aircraft $1,142,500,000; rotary-wing aircraft $2,283,000,000; long-range unmanned aircraft $266,000,000; Offshore Patrol Cutters $4,300,000,000; Fast Response Cutters $1,000,000,000; Polar Security Cutters $4,300,000,000; Arctic Security Cutters $3,500,000,000; light/medium icebreakers $816,000,000; Waterways Commerce Cutters $162,000,000; shore facilities $4,379,000,000; depot maintenance/C4 $2,200,000,000; maritime domain awareness $170,000,000; autonomous maritime systems $75,000,000. Largest single Coast Guard infusion in history. Budget process waiver of 31 USC 1131-1133 and 1156.

nodes.title: SEC. 10102 — Modifications to SNAP Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 2015(o). Expands SNAP work requirements to adults up to age 64 (from 49). New exceptions text: '(3) EXCEPTIONS.—Paragraph (2) shall not apply to an individual if the individual is— (A) under 18, or over 65, years of age; (B) medically certified as physically or mentally unfit for employment; (C) a parent or other member of a household with responsibility for a dependent child under 14 years of age; (D) otherwise exempt under subsection (d)(2); (E) a pregnant woman; (F) an Indian or an Urban Indian (as such terms are defined in paragraphs (13) and (28) of section 4 of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act); or (G) a California Indian described in section 809(a) of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act.' Prior law exempted parents of children under 6; new law raises to under 14. Noncontiguous state (AK/HI, not Guam/USVI) exemption requires quarterly progress reports and good-faith compliance plan; sunsets December 31, 2028, cannot be renewed. Waiver requires unemployment rate 'at or above 1.5 times the national unemployment rate.' Prior law: ages 18-49. New law: ages 18-64.

nodes.title: SEC. 20002 — Enhancement of DoD Resources for Shipbuilding
nodes.description: Appropriates approximately $28.456 billion across 36 line items for naval shipbuilding industrial base expansion and warship procurement. Bill text (lines 2418-2499): 'In addition to amounts otherwise available, there are appropriated to the Secretary of Defense for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029.' Key procurements: $4,600,000,000 'for a second Virginia-class submarine in fiscal year 2026'; $5,400,000,000 'for two additional Guided Missile Destroyer (DDG) ships'; $2,725,000,000 for T-AO oilers; $1,534,000,000 'for procurement of Landing Ship Medium'; $1,803,941,000 landing ship; $1,534,000,000 'for expansion of small unmanned surface vessel production'; $2,100,000,000 'for development, procurement, and integration of purpose-built medium unmanned surface vessels'; $1,300,000,000 'for expansion of unmanned underwater vehicle production'; $450,000,000 'for United States additive manufacturing for wire production and machining capacity'; $150,000,000 'for retention of inactive reserve fleet ships'. Three items specified US domestic production: turbine generators, steel plate, and additive manufacturing. No statutory amendments — funds flow through existing authorities. All funds available through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 60001 — Rescission of Funding for Clean Heavy-Duty Vehicles
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 132 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7432) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels all unspent IRA money for the Clean Heavy-Duty Vehicles program (grants/rebates to replace diesel school buses, transit buses, heavy trucks with zero-emission alternatives). IRA originally appropriated $1 billion under Sec. 60101 (PL 117-169, 136 Stat. 2065). Effective on enactment. Losers: school districts, transit agencies, trucking operators, communities near freight corridors with diesel pollution. Program statute (CAA Sec. 132) remains on books; only the unspent appropriation is clawed back.

nodes.title: CFPB funding cut bypasses appropriations process — permanent structural constraint
nodes.description: The CFPB's funding mechanism under 12 U.S.C. 5497 draws directly from Federal Reserve operating expenses, not from annual congressional appropriations. The amendment to Sec. 1017(a)(2)(A)(iii) — striking '12' and inserting '6.5' — therefore does not require annual legislative action to maintain its effect. The cut is immediate and permanent unless Congress later amends the statute. Unlike an appropriations rider, this cannot be reversed in a single budget cycle without affirmative legislation. Analysis note: 'There is no phasedown, no adjustment for inflation, and no waiver authority.' Benefits financial institutions regulated by the CFPB (banks, nonbank lenders, debt collectors, credit card companies); harms consumers who rely on CFPB supervision, enforcement actions, and complaint resolution.

nodes.title: SEC. 50101 — Onshore Oil and Gas Leasing
nodes.description: Repeals IRA §50262(a) and (e), restoring pre-IRA onshore royalty rates and noncompetitive leasing authority. Mandates 'immediately resume quarterly onshore oil and gas lease sales in compliance with the Mineral Leasing Act (30 U.S.C. 181 et seq.)'. Requires minimum 4 lease sales per fiscal year in WY, NM, CO, UT, MT, ND, OK, NV, AK — offering 'not less than 50 percent of available parcels nominated for oil and gas development'. Amends §17(a) to require leasing 'not later than 18 months after the date of receipt by the Secretary of an expression of interest'. Key buried provision: leases 'may not require any stipulations or mitigation requirements not included in the approved resource management plan' and 'initiation of an amendment to an approved resource management plan shall not prevent or delay' leasing. Drill permits: 'a single, non-renewable 4-year period.' Commingling: Secretary 'shall approve applications' if operator installs measurement devices within ±2% uncertainty. Royalty dropped from 16.67% (IRA) back to 12.5%. Revenue loss to Treasury.

nodes.title: SEC. 70001 — References to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986
nodes.description: Establishes that all amendments in Title VII refer to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. IRC § 15 rate-change rules do NOT apply to any rate changes made by this title (§ 70001(b)). Effective: immediately upon enactment.

nodes.title: SEC. 20003 — Enhancement of DoD Resources for Integrated Air and Missile Defense
nodes.description: Appropriates approximately $24.413 billion across two subsections for missile defense and layered homeland defense. Bill text (lines 2502-2539). Subsection (a) Next Generation Missile Defense Technologies: $250,000,000 'for development and testing of directed energy capabilities by the Under Secretary for Research and Engineering'; $500,000,000 'for national security space launch infrastructure'; $2,000,000,000 'for air moving target indicator military satellites'; $5,600,000,000 'for development of space-based and boost phase intercept capabilities'; $7,200,000,000 'for the development, procurement, and integration of military space-based sensors'; $2,550,000,000 'for the development, procurement, and integration of military missile defense capabilities'. Subsection (b) Layered Homeland Defense: $2,200,000,000 'for acceleration of hypersonic defense systems'; $800,000,000 'for accelerated development and deployment of next-generation intercontinental ballistic missile defense systems'; $408,000,000 'for Army space and strategic missile test range infrastructure restoration and modernization in the United States Indo-Pacific Command area of operations west of the international dateline'; $1,975,000,000 'for improved ground-based missile defense radars'; $530,000,000 'for the design and construction of Missile Defense Agency missile instrumentation range safety ship'. Subsection (a) total: $18.5B. Subsection (b) total: $5.913B. The $5.6B for space-based/boost-phase intercept is unprecedented in scale — represents shift from ground-based to space-based kill architecture. All funds available through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 10103 — Availability of Standard Utility Allowances Based on Receipt of Energy Assistance
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 2014(e)(6)(C)(iv)(I) and 7 USC 2014(k)(4). Limits automatic Standard Utility Allowance (SUA) qualification to households WITH an elderly or disabled member. Inserts 'with an elderly or disabled member' after 'households' in section 5(e)(6)(C)(iv)(I). Parallel amendment to 5(k)(4): subparagraph (A) adds 'without an elderly or disabled member' before 'shall be'; subparagraph (B) adds 'with an elderly or disabled member' before 'under a State law'. Current practice: states use nominal LIHEAP payments (sometimes ) to trigger SUA for all households. New law: only elderly/disabled households qualify automatically. No deadline specified.

nodes.title: SEC. 30002 — Rescission of Funds for Green and Resilient Retrofit Program for Multifamily Housing
nodes.description: Bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available under section 30002(a) of the Act entitled An Act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of S. Con. Res. 14, approved August 16, 2022 (Public Law 117-169; 136 Stat. 2027) are rescinded.' Rescinds all unobligated balances of the Green and Resilient Retrofit Program (GRRP) for multifamily housing, originally funded at ~.5M under the Inflation Reduction Act. The provision does not amend existing law; it cancels spending authority already enacted. Obligated funds already committed to specific projects are not rescinded — only the unobligated balance is swept to the Treasury immediately upon enactment. The provision does not define which specific projects had already been obligated, leaving HUD to determine what is protected and what is swept. Projects in the pipeline but not yet formally obligated are vulnerable.

nodes.title: SEC. 60002 — Repeal of Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'Section 134 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7434) is repealed and the unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out that section (as in effect on the day before the date of enactment of this Act) are rescinded.' Analysis: Two-step mechanism — statutory REPEAL of 42 U.S.C. 7434 PLUS rescission of unobligated balances. IRA originally appropriated $27 billion total for the GGRF ('Green Bank'). Much already obligated to EPA-selected grantees (Climate United, Power Forward Communities); rescission captures only unobligated portion. Outright statutory repeal means EPA cannot re-obligate funds even if a court later releases frozen money — program authority no longer exists. Active legal disputes over already-obligated funds are not resolved by this text. Losers: CDFIs, green banks, low-income and disadvantaged communities targeted for climate investment.

nodes.title: SEC. 10104 — Restrictions on Internet Expenses
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 2014(e)(6) by adding new subparagraph (E): '(E) RESTRICTIONS ON INTERNET EXPENSES.—Any service fee associated with internet connection shall not be used in computing the excess shelter expense deduction under this paragraph.' Bars internet costs from SNAP shelter deduction. Some states currently include broadband costs. No deadline specified.

nodes.title: SEC. 40002 — Spectrum Auctions
nodes.description: Extends FCC general auction authority through September 30, 2034 (previously expired March 9, 2023). Amends 47 USC 309(j)(11). Bill text: 'complete a system of competitive bidding under this subsection shall expire September 30, 2034, except that, with respect to the electromagnetic spectrum — (A) between the frequencies of 3.1 gigahertz and 3.45 gigahertz, such authority shall not apply; and (B) between the frequencies of 7.4 gigahertz and 8.4 gigahertz, such authority shall not apply.' Mandates FCC auction at least 300 MHz including at least 100 MHz in 3.98-4.2 GHz band within 2 years. NTIA must identify 500 MHz of federal spectrum for reallocation over 4 years. NTIA schedule: 200 MHz within 2 years, remainder by 4 years; FCC auctions: 200 MHz within 4 years, all remainder within 8 years. President has 60-day national security withdrawal window. Appropriates $50,000,000 to NTIA for spectrum analysis through September 30, 2034. NTIA mandate: maximize net proceeds for Treasury.

nodes.title: SEC. 50102 — Offshore Oil and Gas Leasing
nodes.description: Mandates minimum 30 Gulf of America region-wide oil and gas lease sales through 2040: 'not fewer than 1 lease sale in the region... by December 15, 2025; not fewer than 2 lease sales in that region in each of calendar years 2026 through 2039... not fewer than 1 lease sale... in calendar year 2040, which shall be held by March 15, 2040.' Each Gulf sale must offer 'not fewer than 80,000,000 acres.' Cook Inlet Alaska: minimum 6 sales 2026-2028 and 2030-2032, each offering 'not fewer than 1,000,000 acres.' Gulf lease terms locked to 'Gulf of Mexico Outer Continental Shelf Region-Wide Oil and Gas Lease Sale 254 (85 Fed. Reg. 8010 (February 12, 2020))'; royalty 'not less than 12½ percent, but not more than 16⅔ percent.' Repeals IRA §50261 (which had set 18.75% deepwater floor), restoring OCSLA §8(a)(1) with 12.5-16.67% cap. Alaska revenue sharing: 'beginning in fiscal year 2034... 70 percent shall be paid to the State of Alaska; and 30 percent shall be deposited in the Treasury.' Gulf of Mexico Energy Security Act amended: ',000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2034; and ,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2035 through 2055' distributed to states. Offshore commingling: Secretary 'shall approve a request' unless 'conclusive evidence establishes' safety risk or reduced recovery.

nodes.title: SEC. 70101 — Extension and Enhancement of Reduced Rates
nodes.description: Permanently extends TCJA individual income tax rates by amending IRC § 1(j)(1) to strike ', and before January 1, 2026' and retitles subsection from '2018 THROUGH 2025' to 'BEGINNING AFTER 2017'. Locks in 10%, 12%, 22%, 24%, 32%, 35%, 37% brackets permanently. Also amends § 1(j)(3)(B)(i) so inflation adjustments for brackets above 12% and above 22% are calculated separately. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. Revenue cost: ~.2–1.5 trillion over 10 years (original TCJA projection).

nodes.title: SEC. 60003 — Rescission of Funding for Diesel Emissions Reductions
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60104 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2067) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA supplemental appropriation for Diesel Emissions Reduction Act (DERA) — funded retrofits and replacements for older diesel engines. IRA appropriated $60 million. Effective on enactment. Underlying DERA authority in CAA Sec. 793 is unaffected. Losers: fleet operators, port authorities, construction contractors seeking diesel retrofit grants.

nodes.title: SEC. 71101 — Moratorium on MSP Enrollment Streamlining Rule (through Sept 30, 2034)
nodes.description: Prohibits HHS from implementing 88 Fed. Reg. 65230 (Sept. 21, 2023), 'Streamlining Medicaid; Medicare Savings Program Eligibility Determination and Enrollment,' from enactment through September 30, 2034. Freezes: 42 CFR §406.21(c), §435.4, §435.601, §435.911, §435.952. Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396a. ,000,000 appropriated to CMS for FY2026 (shared with SEC. 71102). Would have auto-enrolled ~860,000 low-income Medicare beneficiaries into Medicare Savings Programs, paying their Part B premiums, deductibles, and cost sharing via Medicaid. Estimated loss: –600/year per affected beneficiary.

nodes.title: SEC. 71201 — Limiting Medicare Coverage of Certain Individuals
nodes.description: Title XVIII of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395 et seq.) is amended by adding at the end the following new section: SEC. 1899C. An individual may be entitled to, or enrolled for, benefits under this title only if the individual is—(1) a citizen or national of the United States; (2) an alien who is lawfully admitted for permanent residence under the Immigration and Nationality Act; (3) an alien who has been granted the status of Cuban and Haitian entrant, as defined in section 501(e) of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980 (Public Law 96–422); or (4) an individual who lawfully resides in the United States in accordance with a Compact of Free Association referred to in section 402(b)(2)(G) of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996. APPLICATION TO INDIVIDUALS CURRENTLY ENROLLED: subsection (a) shall apply beginning on the date that is 18 months after such date of enactment. The Commissioner of Social Security shall complete a review not later than 1 year after the date of enactment. Notification shall be made as soon as practicable after such identification and in a manner designed to ensure such individual's comprehension of such notification. [Lines 14238–14286]

nodes.title: SEC. 50103 — Royalties on Extracted Methane
nodes.description: Full text of section: 'Section 50263 of Public Law 117–169 (30 U.S.C. 1727) is repealed.' Single-sentence repeal of the IRA provision that had imposed royalty payments on methane vented or flared from federal oil and gas leases. Eliminates the only direct federal greenhouse gas pricing mechanism on federal land operations. Methane is approximately 80x more potent than CO2 over 20 years. Revenue loss to Treasury from royalties that would have been collected on vented/flared methane. Benefits oil and gas operators who vent or flare methane. Effective immediately upon enactment.

nodes.title: SEC. 20004 — Enhancement of DoD Resources for Munitions and Defense Supply Chain Resiliency
nodes.description: Appropriates approximately $30.5 billion across four subsections for munitions production, missile stockpiles, and critical minerals. Bill text (lines 2543-2726). Subsection (a) 67 line items (~$21.7B): $1,000,000,000 'for the expansion of the one-way attack unmanned aerial systems industrial base'; $1,000,000,000 'for the creation of next-generation automated munitions production factories'; $2,000,000,000 'for additional activities to improve the United States stockpile of critical minerals through the National Defense Stockpile Transaction Fund, authorized by subchapter III of chapter 5 of title 50'; $500,000,000 'for the expansion of the Defense Exportability Features program'; $500,000,000 'for development, production, and integration of counter-unmanned aerial systems programs'; $400,000,000 'for acceleration of hypersonic strike programs'; $688,000,000 'for the development, production, and integration of long-range multi-service cruise missiles'; $1,000,000 'for establishment of the Joint Energetics Transition Office'. Subsection (b): $3,300,000,000 'for grants and purchase commitments made pursuant to the Industrial Base Fund established under section 4817 of title 10'. Subsection (c): $5,000,000,000 'for investments in critical minerals supply chains made pursuant to the Industrial Base Fund established under section 4817 of title 10'. Subsection (d): $500,000,000 to DoD Credit Program Account 'to carry out the capital assistance program, including loans, loan guarantees, and technical assistance, established under section 149(e) of title 10... for critical minerals and related industries'; subsidy 'available to subsidize gross obligations for the principal amount of direct loans... not to exceed $100,000,000,000' — a 200:1 leverage ratio. $500M Defense Exportability Features is an arms-export subsidy embedded in defense appropriations. All funds through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 60004 — Rescission of Funding to Address Air Pollution
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60105 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2067) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for general air pollution monitoring and reduction grants under IRA Sec. 60105, supporting EPA air quality programs beyond specific vehicle programs. IRA appropriated $117 million. Effective on enactment. Losers: state and local air agencies, communities with non-attainment air quality designations.

nodes.title: SEC. 70102 — Extension and Enhancement of Increased Standard Deduction
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 63(c)(7) to permanently extend TCJA standard deduction and raise amounts. Strikes 'and before January 1, 2026'. Replaces $18,000 with $23,625 (head of household/MFJ) and $12,000 with $15,750 (single). Updates inflation base year from 2017 to 2024. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024 (retroactive to TY 2025).

nodes.title: SEC. 10105 — Matching Funds Requirements
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 2013(a) to introduce state cost-sharing for SNAP benefits beginning FY2028, keyed to payment error rates. New paragraph (2)(B) text: 'beginning in fiscal year 2028, if the payment error rate of a State as determined under clause (ii) is— (I) less than 6 percent, the Federal share...shall be 100 percent, and the State share shall be 0 percent; (II) equal to or greater than 6 percent but less than 8 percent...Federal share 95 percent, State share 5 percent; (III) equal to or greater than 8 percent but less than 10 percent...Federal share 90 percent, State share 10 percent; and (IV) equal to or greater than 10 percent...Federal share 85 percent, State share 15 percent.' For FY2028 states may elect to use FY2025 or FY2026 error rate. FY2029+: use error rate from 3 years prior. Delayed implementation if FY2025 error rate x 1.5 >= 20% (to FY2029) or FY2026 error rate x 1.5 >= 20% (to FY2030). Also amends 7 USC 2022(a)(1) to block Secretary from waiving state share obligations: inserts 'or the payment or disposition of a State share under section 4(a)(2)' to limit waiver authority. HISTORIC CHANGE: SNAP benefits have been 100% federally funded since program inception.

nodes.title: SEC. 40003 — Air Traffic Control Improvements
nodes.description: Appropriates $12,520,000,000 to FAA for FY 2025 for air traffic control modernization, available until September 30, 2029. Bill text: 'there is appropriated to the Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029.' Breakdown: telecommunications infrastructure $4,750,000,000; radar systems replacement $3,000,000,000; runway safety/surface surveillance $500,000,000; Enterprise Information Display Systems $300,000,000; weather systems (AWOS/VWOS/cameras) $80,000,000; weather tech (sec 44745) $40,000,000; new ARTCC $1,900,000,000; ARTCC Realignment/Consolidation $100,000,000; TRACON recapitalization $1,000,000,000; unstaffed infrastructure sustainment $350,000,000; FAA Reauth 2024 sec 961 $50,000,000; sec 619 $300,000,000; sec 621/remote towers $50,000,000; controller advanced training $100,000,000. New ARTCC provision: 'not more than 2 percent of such amount is used for planning or administrative purposes: Provided further, That at least 3 existing ARTCCs are divested and integrated into the newly constructed ARTCC.' Realignment: 'at least 10 existing ARTCCs are closed or consolidated.' Quarterly reporting to Congress starting 180 days after enactment.

nodes.title: SEC. 90001 — Border Infrastructure and Wall System
nodes.description: Appropriates $46,550,000,000 to the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for necessary expenses relating to: (1) Construction, installation, or improvement of new or replacement primary, waterborne, and secondary barriers; (2) Access roads; (3) Barrier system attributes, including cameras, lights, sensors, and other detection technology; (4) Any work necessary to prepare the ground at or near the border to allow U.S. Customs and Border Protection to conduct its operations, including the construction and maintenance of the barrier system. Funds are in addition to amounts otherwise available — not subject to ordinary annual appropriations limits.

nodes.title: SEC. 70501 — Termination of Previously-Owned Clean Vehicle Credit
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 25E(g) by striking 'December 31, 2032' and inserting 'September 30, 2025'. Eliminates the $4,000 tax credit for purchasing a used electric vehicle (IRC § 25E). Credit enacted by IRA 2022 § 13401. Ends for vehicles acquired after September 30, 2025. CBO estimated roughly $1 billion/year at full utilization; 7-year early termination is multi-billion reduction. Means-tested: buyers earning under $75k single/$150k joint qualified. No phase-down — abrupt cutoff.

nodes.title: SEC. 60005 — Rescission of Funding to Address Air Pollution at Schools
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60106 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2069) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds specifically designated for monitoring and reducing air pollution at and near K-12 schools in communities with elevated pollution exposure. IRA appropriated $50 million under Sec. 60106. Effective on enactment. Losers: schools in high-pollution areas, children with asthma and respiratory conditions.

nodes.title: SEC. 30002 — IRA rollback: GRRP rescission harms affordable housing and low-income tenants
nodes.description: SEC. 30002 rescinds unobligated GRRP balances (originally ~.5M under IRA, P.L. 117-169). The GRRP provided grants and loans to owners of HUD-assisted multifamily properties for energy-efficiency and climate-resilience retrofits. Loses: owners of HUD-assisted multifamily properties (affordable housing stock) who had pending or planned retrofit projects; low-income tenants who would have benefited from reduced utility costs and improved building quality. 'The provision does not define which specific projects had already been obligated, leaving HUD to determine what is protected and what is swept. Projects in the pipeline but not yet formally obligated are vulnerable.' Fits a broader pattern visible across multiple titles: rescinding unobligated IRA green-energy and climate-resilience spending appropriated in 2022.

nodes.title: SEC. 71201: Four-category immigration framework narrows Medicare eligibility — excludes DACA, TPS, visa holders, certain refugees
nodes.description: The four-category structure (LPRs, Cuban/Haitian entrants, COFA residents, U.S. citizens/nationals) is narrower than existing Medicaid five-year bar framework. Termination of currently enrolled ineligible individuals: 18 months post-enactment (~January 4, 2027). Notice must be 'designed to ensure such individual's comprehension' — potential multilingual notice obligation. COFA residents explicitly protected, reflecting treaty obligations with Micronesia, Marshall Islands, Palau.

nodes.title: SEC. 50104 — Alaska Oil and Gas Leasing (ANWR Coastal Plain)
nodes.description: Mandates 4 additional Coastal Plain (ANWR) area-wide lease sales beyond TCJA requirements, within 10 years. Schedule: 'initial lease sale under paragraph (1) not later than 1 year after the date of enactment'; second by year 3; third by year 5; fourth by year 7. Acreage per sale: 'not fewer than 400,000 acres area-wide' prioritizing 'those areas that have the highest potential for the discovery of hydrocarbons.' Terms locked to '85 Fed. Reg. 51754 (August 21, 2020)' — the 2020 ANWR Record of Decision. Revenue: 'for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2033, 50 percent shall be paid to the State of Alaska; and for fiscal year 2034 and each fiscal year thereafter, 70 percent shall be paid to the State of Alaska; and the balance shall be deposited into the Treasury as miscellaneous receipts.' Highest-potential-hydrocarbon language directs leasing to ecologically sensitive calving grounds of Porcupine caribou herd. Locking to challenged 2020 ROD prevents updated environmental analysis.

nodes.title: SEC. 10106 — Administrative Cost Sharing
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 2025(a). Cuts federal share of SNAP administrative costs from 50% to 25% starting FY2027. Text: 'agency, through fiscal year 2026, 50 percent, and for fiscal year 2027 and each fiscal year thereafter, 25 percent,' (replacing 'agency an amount equal to 50 per centum'). States currently receive 50-50 federal-state match on administrative costs. This halves the federal contribution. National SNAP admin costs run ~-6B/year; shift could cost states ~.5B/year in new expenses. Effective FY2027.

nodes.title: SEC. 90002 — CBP Personnel, Fleet Vehicles, and Facilities
nodes.description: Appropriates ~$12,007,630,000 to the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection for fiscal year 2025, available until September 30, 2029: (1) PERSONNEL: $4,100,000,000 to hire and train additional Border Patrol agents, Office of Field Operations officers, Air and Marine agents, rehired annuitants, and CBP field support personnel; (2) RETENTION, HIRING, AND PERFORMANCE BONUSES: $2,052,630,000 for recruitment bonuses, performance awards, or annual retention bonuses to eligible Border Patrol agents, OFO officers, and Air and Marine agents; (3) VEHICLES: $855,000,000 for repair of existing patrol units and lease or acquisition of additional patrol units; (4) FACILITIES: $5,000,000,000 for lease, acquisition, construction, design, or improvement of facilities and checkpoints owned, leased, or operated by CBP. RESTRICTION (subsec. b): None of the funds may be used to recruit, hire, or train personnel for the duties of processing coordinators after October 31, 2028.

nodes.title: SEC. 71102 — Moratorium on Medicaid/CHIP/BHP Enrollment Streamlining Rule (through Sept 30, 2034)
nodes.description: Prohibits HHS from implementing 89 Fed. Reg. 22780 (April 2, 2024), 'Streamlining the Medicaid, CHIP, and Basic Health Program Application, Eligibility Determination, Enrollment, and Renewal Processes,' from enactment through September 30, 2034. Freezes 42 CFR: §431.213(d), §435.222, §435.407, §435.907, §435.911(c), §435.912, §435.916, §435.919, §435.1200(b)(3)(i)-(v), §435.1200(e)(1)(ii), §435.1200(h)(1), §447.56(a)(1)(v), §457.344, §457.960, §457.1140(d)(4), §457.1170, §457.1180. Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396a, 1397cc, 1397gg. Funded by M shared with SEC. 71101. Would have maintained coverage for 2.5–3.5 million people via ex parte renewals and extended renewal windows. Estimated additional disenrollments: 500,000–1,000,000/year. Freeze of §447.56(a)(1)(v) removes cost sharing exemptions for low-income enrollees.

nodes.title: SEC. 20005 — Enhancement of DoD Resources for Scaling Low-Cost Weapons into Production
nodes.description: Appropriates approximately $14.2 billion for technology scaling, low-cost weapons production, AI/autonomous systems, and a $1B credit facility. Bill text (lines 2730-2826). Subsection (a) 33 line items (~$13.2B): $1,400,000,000 'for the expansion of the small unmanned aerial system industrial base'; $2,000,000,000 'for the expansion of Defense Innovation Unit scaling of commercial technology for military use'; $1,685,000,000 'for military cryptographic modernization activities'; $1,500,000,000 'for the development, procurement, and integration of low-cost cruise missiles'; $1,000,000,000 'for the expansion of programs to accelerate the procurement and fielding of innovative technologies'; $750,000,000 'for the acceleration of innovative military logistics and energy capability development and deployment'; $500,000,000 'to prevent delays in delivery of attritable autonomous military capabilities'; $500,000,000 'for the accelerated development and integration of advanced 5G/6G technologies for military use'; $250,000,000 'for the expansion of Cyber Command artificial intelligence lines of effort'; $250,000,000 'for the acceleration of the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative'; $125,000,000 'for the acceleration of development of small, portable modular nuclear reactors for military use' (no safety/environmental/regulatory framework specified); $50,000,000 'for the development, procurement, and integration of high-altitude stratospheric balloons for military use'. Subsection (b) credit facility: $1,000,000,000 subsidy supporting 'gross obligations for the principal amount of direct loans... not to exceed $100,000,000,000' under 10 U.S.C. § 149(e). All funds through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 60006 — Rescission of Funding for the Low Emissions Electricity Program
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 135 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7435) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for EPA's Low Emissions Electricity Program under CAA Sec. 135, which supported outreach, education, and technical assistance on reducing emissions from electricity generation and use. IRA appropriated $100 million. The statute is NOT repealed — only defunded. Effective on enactment. Losers: state energy offices, utilities, and clean energy educators using EPA guidance materials.

nodes.title: SEC. 70502 — Termination of Clean Vehicle Credit
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 30D(h) striking 'placed in service after December 31, 2032' and inserting 'acquired after September 30, 2025'. Primary EV credit up to $7,500 for new electric vehicles eliminated 7 years early. Conforming amendments to § 30D(e): strikes clause (v) from paragraph (1)(B) and clauses (iv)-(vi) from paragraph (2)(B) — deletes progressive battery domestic content percentage requirements (battery sourcing thresholds for 2029+). CBO estimated $7.5 billion/year at peak; termination saves $50+ billion over original window. Abrupt cutoff — no phase-down. Credit had transferred point-of-sale to dealers under IRA.

nodes.title: SEC. 70301 — Full Expensing for Certain Business Property
nodes.description: Permanently restores 100% bonus depreciation (full expensing) for qualifying business property under IRC §168(k). Amends §168(k)(2)(A) by striking clause (iii) (phasedown trigger); amends §168(k)(1)(A) by replacing 'applicable percentage' with '100 percent'; strikes §168(k) paragraphs (6) and (8) (phasedown tables). Transitional election for first taxable year ending after January 19, 2025: taxpayers may elect 40% (regular property) or 60% (long-production-period/transportation property). Specified plants (orchards/vineyards) covered — removes 'planted before January 1, 2027' sunset. Effective: property acquired after January 19, 2025 (retroactive to inauguration day). JCT revenue cost estimated –500B over 10 years. §460(c)(6)(B) amended for 7-year recovery period property.

nodes.title: SEC. 100001 — APPLICABILITY OF THE IMMIGRATION LAWS (8 U.S.C. 1801)
nodes.description: Boilerplate applicability provision establishing that INA definitions govern all terms in the fee subtitle. Terms used under this subtitle shall have the meanings given such terms in section 101 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101). References to INA sections are cross-references throughout the subtitle. New codification at 8 U.S.C. 1801 et seq. No money, no deadlines, no waivers — purely administrative. Lines 16794-16804 of bigbill.txt.

nodes.title: SEC. 71202 — Temporary Payment Increase Under the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule to Account for Exceptional Circumstances
nodes.description: Section 1848(t) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1395w–4(t)) is amended: (1) in the subsection heading, by striking 'DURING 2021 THROUGH 2024'; (2) in paragraph (1), by striking 'and 2024' and inserting '2024, and 2026'; (D) by adding at the end: '(F) such services furnished on or after January 1, 2026, and before January 1, 2027, by 2.5 percent.' CONFORMING AMENDMENT: Section 1848(c)(2)(B)(iv)(V) is amended by striking 'or 2024' and inserting '2024, or 2026'. Extends exceptional circumstances 2.5% physician payment bump to CY2026. Conforming amendment prevents temporary increase from triggering MACRA feedback loop. [Lines 14290–14314]

nodes.title: SEC. 80001 / Subtitle A — Exemption of Certain Assets
nodes.description: Amends HEA §480(f)(2) (20 U.S.C. 1087vv(f)(2)) to add three new excluded asset categories from financial aid need analysis: '(B) a family farm on which the family resides; (C) a small business with not more than 100 full-time or full-time equivalent employees (or any part of such a small business) that is owned and controlled by the family; or (D) a commercial fishing business and related expenses, including fishing vessels and permits owned and controlled by the family.' Effective July 1, 2026; applies to award year 2026–2027 and each subsequent award year. No direct appropriation. Benefits rural families, farmers, commercial fishermen, and small-business owners whose productive assets previously counted against financial aid eligibility.

nodes.title: SEC. 50105 — National Petroleum Reserve–Alaska
nodes.description: Restores and mandates NPR-A oil and gas leasing, suspended under Biden. Effective on enactment: 'the Secretary shall expeditiously restore and resume oil and gas lease sales under the Program.' Mandates 5 lease sales within 10 years: initial 'not later than 1 year after the date of enactment' then 'not later than every 2 years.' Each sale: 'not fewer than 4,000,000 acres.' Terms locked to 'National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska Integrated Activity Plan Final Environmental Impact Statement... dated June 2020, including the errata sheet dated October 6, 2020, and EXCLUDING the errata sheet dated September 20, 2022.' The September 2022 errata exclusion is the critical buried provision — that errata had added Special Areas protections for ~13 million acres of the most ecologically sensitive NPR-A land; excluding it reopens those acres to leasing. Revenue sharing: beginning FY2034, '70 percent shall be paid to the State of Alaska; and 30 percent shall be paid into the Treasury.' Federal share drops from standard rate to 30%.

nodes.title: SEC. 90003 — Detention Capacity
nodes.description: Appropriates $45,000,000,000 to U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for single adult alien detention capacity and family residential center capacity. DURATION AND STANDARDS (subsec. b): Aliens may be detained at family residential centers pending a decision under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.) on whether the aliens are to be removed from the United States and, if such aliens are ordered removed, until such aliens are removed. Detention standards for single adult facilities shall be set in the discretion of the Secretary of Homeland Security, consistent with applicable law. DEFINITION (subsec. c): 'family residential center' means a facility used by DHS to detain family units of aliens (including alien children who are not unaccompanied alien children as defined in section 462(g) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 279(g))) who are encountered or apprehended by DHS.

nodes.title: SEC. 40004 — Space Launch and Reentry Licensing and Permitting User Fees
nodes.description: Creates new 51 USC 50924 establishing per-launch user fee system for FAA-licensed commercial space launches starting 2026. Fee is lesser of per-pound payload rate or flat cap: 2026 $0.25/lb capped at $30,000; 2027 $0.35/lb capped at $40,000; 2028 $0.50/lb capped at $50,000; 2029 $0.60/lb capped at $75,000; 2030 $0.75/lb capped at $100,000; 2031 $1.00/lb capped at $125,000; 2032 $1.25/lb capped at $170,000; 2033 $1.50/lb capped at $200,000; 2034+ CPI-indexed. Bill text: 'The Secretary of Transportation shall impose a fee...on each launch or reentry carried out under a license or permit issued under section 50904 during 2026 or a subsequent year, in an amount equal to the lesser of — (A) the amount specified in paragraph (2) for the year involved per pound of the weight of the payload; or (B) the amount specified in paragraph (3) for the year involved.' Establishes Office of Commercial Space Transportation Launch and Reentry Licensing and Permitting Fund: '70 percent of the amounts deposited into the fund shall be available for such purposes and shall be available without further appropriation and without fiscal year limitation.' 30% flows to Treasury. Applicable to SpaceX, Rocket Lab, ULA, Blue Origin. Heavy-lift vehicles (Falcon 9 ~22,000 kg) will almost always hit the flat cap.

nodes.title: SEC. 30003 — Securities and Exchange Commission Reserve Fund
nodes.description: Bill text: (a) IN GENERAL — Section 4 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78d) is amended — (1) by striking subsection (i); and (2) by redesignating subsections (j) and (k) as subsections (i) and (j), respectively. (b) TECHNICAL AND CONFORMING AMENDMENT — Section 21F(g)(2) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78u-6(g)(2)) is amended to read: 'The Fund shall be available to the Commission, without further appropriation or fiscal year limitation, for paying awards to whistleblowers as provided in subsection (b).' (c) TRANSITION PROVISION — During the period beginning on the date of enactment and ending on October 1, 2025, the SEC may expend amounts in the Reserve Fund that were obligated before enactment for any ongoing program, project, or activity. (d) TRANSFER OF REMAINING AMOUNTS — Effective October 1, 2025, the obligated and unobligated balances in the SEC Reserve Fund shall be transferred to the general fund of the Treasury. (e) CLOSING OF ACCOUNT — The Reserve Fund shall be considered closed upon execution of the transfer, and shall not be available for obligation or expenditure for any purpose. Reserve Fund had statutory cap of M; whistleblower award fund is preserved.

nodes.title: SEC. 70503 — Termination of Qualified Commercial Clean Vehicles Credit
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 45W(g) striking 'December 31, 2032' and inserting 'September 30, 2025'. Terminates credit for businesses purchasing electric or other clean commercial vehicles (trucks, vans, buses). Credit was worth up to $40,000 per vehicle for large trucks. Enacted by IRA 2022 § 13403. CBO estimated approximately $3 billion/year. Vehicles must be acquired on or before September 30, 2025. Loses: fleet operators (trucking, delivery, transit agencies), commercial EV manufacturers (Rivian Commercial, BrightDrop, Lion Electric), municipalities that planned electric bus fleets.

nodes.title: SEC. 60007 — Rescission of Funding for Section 211(o) of the Clean Air Act
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60108 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2070) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS) implementation under CAA Sec. 211(o), governing biofuel blending requirements and EPA's administration of the RFS program. IRA appropriated $20 million under Sec. 60108. The RFS program itself is not repealed. Effective on enactment. Losers: biofuel producers, EPA's RFS administrative capacity.

nodes.title: SEC. 71103 — Reducing Duplicate Enrollment Under Medicaid and CHIP
nodes.description: Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396a (§1902) adding paragraphs (88) and subsections (uu) and (vv); amends 42 U.S.C. 1396b(r)(3) (PARIS system); amends 42 U.S.C. 1396u-2 (§1932 new subsection (j)); amends 42 U.S.C. 1397cc(f)(3), 1397gg(e)(1). Creates two systems: (1) Address tracking (subsection vv): states must obtain address info from USPS forwarding mail, National Change of Address Database, managed care entities, other Secretary-approved sources. Beginning Jan 1, 2027. MCOs must transmit address changes to states beginning Jan 1, 2027. (2) Cross-state duplicate enrollment system (subsection uu): CMS must build national database by Oct 1, 2029. States must submit SSNs monthly. System flags dual-enrollment; states must disenroll individuals not residing in state. Appropriations: ,000,000 FY2026 to build system; ,000,000 FY2029 to maintain it. Creates centralized federal registry of all Medicaid enrollees' SSNs — significant privacy implications. Privacy standard only: 'consistent with subsection (a)(7).' No additional data security requirements specified.

nodes.title: SEC. 50201 — Coal Leasing
nodes.description: Defines 'qualified application' as pending coal lease applications as of enactment or filed within 90 days. Requires Interior within 90 days to: '(i) if not previously published for public comment, publish any required environmental review; (ii) establish the fair market value of the applicable coal tract; (iii) hold a lease sale with respect to the applicable coal tract; and (iv) identify the highest bidder at or above the fair market value.' May also grant any approvals required for mining to commence on previously-issued leases. NEPA preserved in form but 90-day mandatory timeline makes substantive review functionally impossible for complex sites. Rapid coal lease processing removes backlog. Benefits coal industry.

nodes.title: SEC. 20006 — Enhancement of DoD Resources for Efficiency and Cybersecurity
nodes.description: Appropriates $380,000,000 to accelerate the long-delayed DoD financial statement audit and fund DARPA cybersecurity research. Bill text (lines 2830-2848): 'In addition to amounts otherwise available, there are appropriated to the Secretary of Defense for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029.' Line items: $150,000,000 'for business systems replacement to accelerate the audits of the financial statements of the Department of Defense pursuant to chapter 9A and section 2222 of title 10'; $200,000,000 'for the deployment of automation and artificial intelligence to accelerate the audits of the financial statements of the Department of Defense pursuant to chapter 9A and section 2222 of title 10'; $10,000,000 'for the improvement of the budgetary and programmatic infrastructure of the Office of the Secretary of Defense'; $20,000,000 'for defense cybersecurity programs of the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency'. Statutory basis: 10 U.S.C. ch. 9A (DoD financial management) and 10 U.S.C. § 2222 (financial management systems). DoD has failed every audit since 2018; this appropriation funds the audit acceleration effort. All funds through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 70302 — Full Expensing of Domestic Research and Experimental Expenditures
nodes.description: Creates new IRC §174A for 'domestic research or experimental expenditures' — immediate full deduction in year paid. Reverses TCJA 2017 requirement to amortize R&D over 5 years (domestic) / 15 years (foreign). §174 retained but renamed for FOREIGN R&D only — still amortized over 15 years. Software development explicitly treated as R&D under §174A. Optional election: amortize domestic R&D over not less than 60 months. Treated as §481 accounting method change, cut-off basis, no §481(a) adjustment, for years beginning after December 31, 2024. Small business retroactive election: §448(c) gross receipts test companies may elect retroactive application back to December 31, 2021 (must file amended returns; election window is 1 year from enactment by approximately July 4, 2026). Unamortized pre-2025 amounts: may elect to deduct remaining capitalized domestic R&D all in first year after 2024, or ratably over 2 years. Coordinates with §41 R&D credit: §280C(c)(1) reduces §174A deduction by §41(a) credit amount. AMT §56(b)(2) updated. General effective: tax years beginning after December 31, 2024. JCT revenue cost estimated –250B over 10 years.

nodes.title: SEC. 71203 — Expanding and Clarifying the Exclusion for Orphan Drugs Under the Drug Price Negotiation Program
nodes.description: Section 1192(e) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 1320f–1(e)) is amended: (1) in paragraph (1), by striking 'and (3)' and inserting 'through (4)'; (2) in paragraph (3)(A), (A) by striking 'only one rare disease or condition' and inserting 'one or more rare diseases or conditions'; and (B) by striking 'such disease or condition' and inserting 'one or more such rare diseases or conditions (as such term is defined in section 526(a)(2) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act)'; (3) by adding at the end: '(4) TREATMENT OF FORMER ORPHAN DRUGS.—In the case of a drug or biological product that, as of the date of the approval or licensure of such drug or biological product, is a drug or biological product described in paragraph (3)(A), paragraph (1)(A)(ii) or (1)(B)(ii) (as applicable) shall apply as if the reference to the date of such approval were instead a reference to the first day after the date of such approval for which such drug is not a drug described in paragraph (3)(A).' APPLICATION: amendments apply with respect to initial price applicability years beginning on or after January 1, 2028. [Lines 14315–14348]

nodes.title: SEC. 10107 — National Education and Obesity Prevention Grant Program
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 2036a(d)(1)(F). Sunsets SNAP Education/Obesity Prevention Grant Program after FY2025. Strikes 'for fiscal year 2016 and each subsequent fiscal year' and inserts 'for each of fiscal years 2016 through 2025'. Prior law: permanent ongoing mandatory funding. New law: program authority expires after FY2025. Eliminates SNAP-Ed grants that states and localities use for nutrition education. Program sunsets without requiring an affirmative vote to eliminate — change is accomplished by simple date restriction in mandatory funding language.

nodes.title: SEC. 90004 — Border Security, Technology, and Screening
nodes.description: Appropriates $6,168,000,000 to the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection for fiscal year 2025, available until September 30, 2029, for: (1) Procurement and integration of new nonintrusive inspection equipment including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and other innovative technologies to combat illicit narcotics at ports of entry and along southwest, northern, and maritime borders; (2) Air and Marine operations upgrading and procurement of new platforms for rapid air and marine response; (3) Upgrades and procurement of border surveillance technologies along southwest, northern, and maritime borders; (4) Biometric entry and exit system under section 7208 of the Intelligence Reform and Terrorism Prevention Act of 2004 (8 U.S.C. 1365b); (5) Screening persons entering or exiting the United States; (6) Initial screenings of unaccompanied alien children consistent with the William Wilberforce Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2008 (Pub. L. 110-457); (7) Enhancing border security by combating drug trafficking including fentanyl at southwest, northern, and maritime borders; (8) Commemorating efforts and events related to border security. RESTRICTION (subsec. b): None of the funds may be used for procurement or deployment of surveillance towers that have not been tested and accepted by CBP to deliver autonomous capabilities. DEFINITION (subsec. c): 'autonomous' means a system designed to apply AI, machine learning, computer vision, or other algorithms to detect, identify, classify, and track items of interest in real time such that the system can make operational adjustments without the active engagement of personnel or continuous human command or control.

nodes.title: SEC. 100002 — ASYLUM FEE (8 U.S.C. 1802)
nodes.description: Creates mandatory, non-waivable fee on every asylum applicant under INA § 208 (8 U.S.C. 1158). Verbatim text (lines 16805-16854): 'the Secretary of Homeland Security or the Attorney General, as applicable, shall require the payment of a fee, equal to the amount specified in this section, by any alien who files an application for asylum under section 208 (8 U.S.C. 1158) at the time such application is filed.' INITIAL AMOUNT: 'the greater of— (1) ; or (2) such amount as the Secretary or the Attorney General, as applicable, may establish, by rule.' ANNUAL CPI ADJUSTMENT: 'the product resulting from the multiplication of the amount referred to in paragraph (1) by the percentage (if any) by which the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers for the month of July preceding the date on which such adjustment takes effect exceeds the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers for the same month of the preceding calendar year, rounded to the next lowest multiple of $10.' DISPOSITION: 50% to EOIR (AG cases) or 50% to USCIS Immigration Examinations Fee Account (DHS cases); remainder to general fund of Treasury. NO FEE WAIVER: 'Fees required to be paid under this section shall not be waived or reduced.' First-ever filing fee for U.S. asylum applications. Effective FY2025. Cross-refs: INA § 208 (8 U.S.C. 1158); § 286(m) (8 U.S.C. 1356(m)).

nodes.title: SEC. 70504 — Termination of Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Credit
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 30C(i) striking 'December 31, 2032' and inserting 'June 30, 2026'. Terminates 30% tax credit for installing EV charging stations and other alternative fuel refueling equipment (hydrogen, natural gas, propane). Termination is six months later than the EV credits above. Property placed in service after June 30, 2026 does not qualify. Given construction lead times, projects must begin and complete within calendar year 2025 to be safe. Loses: EV charging networks (ChargePoint, Blink, EVgo, Tesla Supercharger third-party), hydrogen fueling operators, CNG/LNG stations. Credit covered not just EV chargers but hydrogen fuel cell and CNG/LNG stations — termination also kills subsidies for some fossil-fuel-adjacent alternative fuel infrastructure.

nodes.title: SEC. 30003 — SEC loses off-budget reserve; whistleblower fund preserved but conforming amendment restructures cross-reference
nodes.description: Eliminating Section 4(i) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (15 U.S.C. 78d(i)) strips the SEC of its off-budget Reserve Fund, which allowed it to retain excess fees (beyond appropriated budget) and spend them without further congressional approval on technology, infrastructure, and inspections. The SEC now loses financial flexibility for technology modernization, EDGAR upgrades, and emergency expenditures without congressional approval. Congress gains restored appropriations control — the SEC can no longer spend outside regular appropriations. The whistleblower award fund (Sec. 21F) is technically amended but the conforming change reaffirms the fund 'shall be available to the Commission, without further appropriation or fiscal year limitation, for paying awards to whistleblowers' — the whistleblower program itself is preserved. Buried: 'any ongoing SEC projects that were mid-stream but not yet formally obligated lose their funding pipeline.' Reserve Fund had historical balances in the tens of millions with a statutory M cap.

nodes.title: SEC. 71203: 'One or more' orphan drug change compounds with clock reset — shields blockbuster drugs from Medicare price negotiation indefinitely
nodes.description: Previously, a drug lost orphan exclusion if approved for multiple conditions where only one was rare. Under new language, any drug with at least one orphan designation retains the exclusion. The 'former orphan drug' clock provision: a drug that held orphan status at approval gets its negotiation clock reset to the date it loses that status, potentially delaying negotiation by years. Fiscal impact could be significant for high-cost multi-indication drugs. Effective: initial price applicability years beginning on or after January 1, 2028.

nodes.title: SEC. 40005 — Mars Missions, Artemis Missions, and Moon to Mars Program
nodes.description: Appropriates $9,995,000,000 to NASA for FY 2025, available until September 30, 2032. New 51 USC 20306. Bill text: 'there is appropriated to the Administration for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, $9,995,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2032.' Breakdown: (1) Mars telecommunications orbiter $700,000,000 — 'procurement, using a competitively bid, firm fixed-price contract with a United States commercial provider...selected from among the commercial proposals that — received funding from the Administration in fiscal year 2024 or 2025 for commercial design studies for Mars Sample Return'; delivered by December 31, 2028; (2) Gateway lunar station $2,600,000,000 — min $750M/yr FY 2026-2028; (3) SLS for Artemis IV and V $4,100,000,000 — min $1,025M/yr FY 2026-2029; (4) Orion for Artemis IV $20,000,000; (5) ISS operations $1,250,000,000 — min $250M/yr FY 2025-2029; (6) manned spaceflight center infrastructure $1,000,000,000 (Stennis $120M, Kennedy $250M, Johnson $300M, Marshall $100M, Michoud $30M, space vehicle transfer $85M); (7) contract 80JSC024CA002 $325,000,000. Space vehicle transfer: 'transferred to a field center...involved in the administration of the Commercial Crew Program...placed on public exhibition at an entity within the Metropolitan Statistical Area' — widely understood as Crew Dragon near KSC. Obligation schedule: 50% by Sep 30, 2028; 100% by Sep 30, 2029; all outlays by Sep 30, 2034.

nodes.title: SEC. 50202 — Coal Royalty
nodes.description: Amends 30 U.S.C. 207(a), fourth sentence: strikes '12½ per centum' and inserts '12½ percent, except such amount shall be not more than 7 percent during the period that begins on the date of enactment... and ends September 30, 2034.' Applicability: 'shall apply to a coal lease issued... before, on, or after the date of the enactment of this Act... that has not been terminated.' Retroactive credit provision: 'the Secretary of the Interior shall provide to the lessee a credit for the difference between the amount paid by the lessee in advance royalties... before the date of the enactment of this Act and the amount the lessee would have been required to pay if the amendment... had been made before the lessee paid advance royalties.' Federal coal royalty cut ~44% from 12.5% to 7% on all active leases. Retroactive credit is effectively a direct federal payment back to coal companies. Combined with §50201 (leasing) and §50203 (new acres), forms three-part coal subsidy package. State revenue shares (normally 50% of royalties under 30 U.S.C. 191) also cut proportionally.

nodes.title: SEC. 70303 — Modification of Limitation on Business Interest
nodes.description: Permanently restores EBITDA-based calculation for §163(j) business interest expense limitation. Amends §163(j)(8)(A)(v) by striking 'in the case of taxable years beginning before January 1, 2022' — making depreciation and amortization add-back to adjusted taxable income (ATI) permanent. Before TCJA: EBITDA basis allowed. Post-2021 under TCJA: EBIT basis (no D&A add-back), dramatically restricting interest deductions for capital-intensive businesses. Also extends floor plan financing exception (§163(j)(9)(C)) to 'any trailer or camper which is designed to provide temporary living quarters for recreational, camping, or seasonal use and is designed to be towed by, or affixed to, a motor vehicle' — covering RV dealers. Effective: tax years beginning after December 31, 2024. Large revenue cost for real estate, utilities, telecom, private equity portfolio companies.

nodes.title: SEC. 60008 — Rescission of Funding for Implementation of the American Innovation and Manufacturing Act
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60109 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2071) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for EPA's implementation of the AIM Act, which phases down hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) production and consumption — potent greenhouse gases used in refrigerants and air conditioning. IRA appropriated $60 million under Sec. 60109. The AIM Act phasedown schedule is not altered. BURIED PROVISION: Defunding enforcement of the AIM Act without repealing it creates a gap between legal obligation and administrative capacity. Effective on enactment. Beneficiaries: HFC manufacturers.

nodes.title: SEC. 71104 — Ensuring Deceased Individuals Do Not Remain Enrolled
nodes.description: Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396a (§1902) adding paragraph (89) and new subsection (ww). Beginning January 1, 2027, states must, not less frequently than quarterly, review the Death Master File (defined in Bipartisan Budget Act of 2013 §203(d)) for all enrollees. If Death Master File indicates individual is deceased: state shall (i) treat such information as 'factual information confirming the death of a beneficiary'; (ii) disenroll in accordance with §1902(a)(3); (iii) discontinue payments except for items/services furnished prior to death. Reinstatement: if misidentified, state must 'immediately re-enroll such individual...retroactive to the date of such disenrollment.' No timeline specified for processing reinstatement. Known Death Master File error rate: ~0.5–1%, meaning quarterly checks on ~80M enrollees could generate 400,000–800,000 erroneous disenrollment events per cycle. Elderly, disabled, hospitalized individuals with common names most vulnerable.

nodes.title: SEC. 20007 — Enhancement of DoD Resources for Air Superiority
nodes.description: Appropriates approximately $8.6 billion across 19 line items for aircraft procurement, retirement prevention, and next-generation air dominance. Bill text (lines 2851-2885): 'In addition to amounts otherwise available, there are appropriated to the Secretary of Defense for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029.' Line items: $3,150,000,000 'to increase F-15EX aircraft production'; $361,220,000 'to prevent the retirement of F-22 aircraft'; $127,460,000 'to prevent the retirement of F-15E aircraft'; $678,000,000 'to accelerate the Collaborative Combat Aircraft program'; $400,000,000 'to accelerate production of the F-47 aircraft' (publicly acknowledged only March 2025 — early-stage funding with minimal program definition in text); $750,000,000 'accelerate the FA/XX aircraft'; $474,000,000 'to increase EA-37B production'; $440,000,000 'to increase C-130J production'; $270,000,000 'for development, procurement, and integration of Marine Corps unmanned combat aircraft'; $600,000,000 'for the development, procurement, and integration of Air Force long-range strike aircraft'; $500,000,000 'for the development, procurement, and integration of Navy long-range strike aircraft'. Blocking planned F-22 and F-15E retirements while simultaneously funding NGAD — spreads resources rather than concentrating them on next-gen. No statutory amendments. All funds through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 70505 — Termination of Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 25C(h) striking 'placed in service' and all through 'December 31, 2032' and inserting 'placed in service after December 31, 2025'. Terminates 30% credit (up to $3,200/year) for home energy improvements — heat pumps, insulation, efficient doors/windows, electrical panel upgrades, energy audits. Also amends § 25C(d)(2)(C): changes oil furnace/boiler standard, replacing requirement for fuel blends at least 50% eligible fuel with 20%. New text: 'Any oil furnace or hot water boiler which (i) meets or exceeds 2021 Energy Star efficiency criteria, and (ii) is rated by the manufacturer for use with fuel blends at least 20 percent of the volume of which consists of an eligible fuel.' CBO estimated approximately $6 billion/year; terminating saves ~$42 billion over 7-year window. Enacted by IRA 2022 § 13301. Fuel blend change: quiet deregulatory gift to oil heating industry — loosens the standard for what qualifies as eligible oil furnace just as credit ends.

nodes.title: SEC. 90005 — State and Local Assistance
nodes.description: Two parts. (a) STATE HOMELAND SECURITY GRANT PROGRAMS: Appropriates $2,575,000,000 to the Administrator of FEMA for fiscal year 2025, available until September 30, 2029, under the State Homeland Security Grant Program (6 U.S.C. 605): (A) $500,000,000 for State and local capabilities to detect, identify, track, or monitor threats from unmanned aircraft systems (49 U.S.C. 44801); (B) $625,000,000 for security and other costs related to the 2026 FIFA World Cup; (C) $1,000,000,000 for security, planning, and other costs related to the 2028 Olympics; (D) $450,000,000 for the Operation Stonegarden Grant Program. FIFA and Olympics grants exempted from requirements of 6 U.S.C. 605(e)(1) and 6 U.S.C. 609(a)(12). (b) STATE BORDER SECURITY REINFORCEMENT FUND (8 U.S.C. 1716): Establishes fund within DHS. Purposes: (A) Construction or installation of a border wall, border fencing or other barrier, or buoys along the southern border; (B) Any work necessary to prepare the ground at or near land borders; (C) Detection and interdiction of illicit substances and aliens who have unlawfully entered and committed a crime; (D) Relocation of aliens who are unlawfully present in the United States from small population centers to other domestic locations. Appropriates $10,000,000,000 available until September 30, 2034. ELIGIBILITY: grants available for expenditures made for activities that occurred on or after January 20, 2021. Applications accepted within 90 days of enactment. FEMA may use up to 1 percent for administration.

nodes.title: SEC. 10108 — Alien SNAP Eligibility
nodes.description: Completely rewrites 7 USC 2015(f) (Section 6(f) of Food and Nutrition Act of 2008). New text: 'No individual who is a member of a household otherwise eligible to participate in the supplemental nutrition assistance program under this section shall be eligible to participate in the supplemental nutrition assistance program as a member of that or any other household unless he or she is— (1) a resident of the United States; and (2) either— (A) a citizen or national of the United States; (B) an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence as an immigrant as defined by sections 101(a)(15) and 101(a)(20) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, excluding, among others, alien visitors, tourists, diplomats, and students who enter the United States temporarily with no intention of abandoning their residence in a foreign country; (C) an alien who has been granted the status of Cuban and Haitian entrant, as defined in section 501(e) of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980 (Public Law 96-422); or (D) an individual who lawfully resides in the United States in accordance with a Compact of Free Association referred to in section 402(b)(2)(G) of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996. The income (less, at State option, a pro rata share) and financial resources of the individual rendered ineligible to participate in the supplemental nutrition assistance program under this subsection shall be considered in determining the eligibility and the value of the allotment of the household of which such individual is a member.' REMOVES eligibility for: refugees (INA §207), asylees (INA §208), deportation-withheld individuals, Amerasians, non-citizen veterans and active duty military and their dependents, trafficking victims, Iraqi/Afghan special immigrants, PRWORA qualified immigrants who completed 5-year wait. The income-counting rule at the end means ineligible household members' income still counts against eligible members — double penalty for mixed-status households.

nodes.title: SEC. 60009 — Rescission of Funding for Enforcement Technology and Public Information
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60110 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2071) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for EPA's environmental enforcement technology upgrades and public information systems, including tools for tracking violations and communicating regulatory data to the public. IRA appropriated $5 million under Sec. 60110. Effective on enactment. Losers: EPA enforcement offices; public access to violation data may be degraded. Beneficiaries: regulated industries facing less scrutiny.

nodes.title: SEC. 100003 — EMPLOYMENT AUTHORIZATION DOCUMENT FEES (8 U.S.C. 1803)
nodes.description: Three subsections creating new EAD fees. (a) ASYLUM APPLICANTS: 'the Secretary of Homeland Security shall require the payment of a fee... by any alien who files an initial application for employment authorization under section 208(d)(2) (8 U.S.C. 1158(d)(2)) at the time such initial employment authorization application is filed.' Fee: greater of $550 or higher by rule; CPI-indexed annually rounded to next lowest $10. Disposition: 25% to USCIS (Immigration Examinations Fee Account under § 286(m)); 'not less than 50 percent [of that 25%] is used to detect and prevent immigration benefit fraud'; remainder to general Treasury. NO FEE WAIVER. (b) PAROLEES: $550 initial fee; 'Each initial employment authorization shall be valid for a period of 1 year or for the duration of the alien's parole, whichever is shorter.' 100% to general Treasury. NO FEE WAIVER. (c) TEMPORARY PROTECTED STATUS: $550 initial fee; EAD 'valid for a period of 1 year, or for the duration of the alien's temporary protected status, whichever is shorter.' 100% to general Treasury. NO FEE WAIVER. 1-year validity cap forces perpetual renewal fees. Lines 16855-16972. Cross-refs: INA §§ 208(d)(2), 244(a)(1)(B), 286(m).

nodes.title: SEC. 30004 — Appropriations for Defense Production Act
nodes.description: Bill text: 'In addition to amounts otherwise available, there is appropriated for fiscal year 2025, out of amounts not otherwise appropriated, ,000,000,000, to remain available until September 30, 2027, to carry out the Defense Production Act (50 U.S.C. 4501 et seq.).' Direct appropriation of B for FY 2025, available for two years through September 30, 2027. Does not amend existing law; provides funding for existing DPA authority. The DPA grants the executive branch broad authority to direct industrial production, prioritize contracts, and expand domestic capacity for national defense and critical supply chains. Congress provides no further direction on which industries or programs must receive funding — allocation is entirely at executive discretion. Benefits: defense contractors and domestic manufacturers (DPA-directed orders or incentives); industries identified as critical supply chains (semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, rare earth minerals); the executive branch gains significant discretionary authority. Marked 'Expiration date' in margin of enrolled bill.

nodes.title: SEC. 50203 — Leases for Known Recoverable Coal Resources
nodes.description: 'Notwithstanding section 2(a)(3)(A) of the Mineral Leasing Act (30 U.S.C. 201(a)(3)(A)) and section 202(a) of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (43 U.S.C. 1712(a)), not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Interior shall make available for lease known recoverable coal resources of not less than 4,000,000 additional acres on Federal land.' Exclusions: National Monuments, National Recreation Areas, Wilderness System, Wild and Scenic Rivers, National Trails, National Conservation Areas, National Wildlife Refuge System, National Fish Hatchery System, National Park System. All other BLM and Forest Service land presumptively eligible. 'Notwithstanding FLPMA §202' language bypasses the statutory land-use planning process.
