No tribal consultation, local government input, or public participation required within 90-day window.

nodes.title: SEC. 71105 — Ensuring Deceased Providers Do Not Remain Enrolled
nodes.description: Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396a(kk)(1) adding new subparagraph (B). Beginning January 1, 2028: at enrollment, reenrollment, and revalidation of enrollment, and not less frequently than quarterly during enrollment period, state must check the Death Master File (Bipartisan Budget Act of 2013 §203(d)) for each provider/supplier. Addresses fraud vector of billing under deceased provider numbers. Affects approximately 1 million Medicaid-enrolled providers. No specific appropriation.

nodes.title: SEC. 81001 / Subtitle B — Loan Limits: Termination of Grad PLUS, New Caps
nodes.description: Amends HEA §455(a) (20 U.S.C. 1087e(a)). TERMINATES Graduate/Professional PLUS loans effective July 1, 2026: 'for any period of instruction beginning on or after July 1, 2026, a graduate or professional student shall not be eligible to receive a Federal Direct PLUS Loan under this part.' Annual limits beginning July 1, 2026: graduate non-professional $20,500/year; professional student $50,000/year. Aggregate limits: non-professional grad $100,000; professional $200,000 (both tracks share $200,000 combined). Parent PLUS: '$20,000' annual per dependent; '$65,000, without regard to any amounts repaid, forgiven, canceled, or otherwise discharged' aggregate lifetime per dependent. Overall student lifetime cap: '$257,500, without regard to any amounts repaid, forgiven, canceled, or otherwise discharged.' Part-time enrollment: loans 'reduced in direct proportion.' Institutions may impose lower limits 'applied consistently to all students enrolled in such program.' Grandfather: students enrolled as of June 30, 2026 protected for 'the lesser of three academic years; or the period determined by calculating the difference between the program length and the period of such program of study that such individual has completed.' Medical students face shortfall: costs $60-80K/year over 4 years vs $200K lifetime cap. ~$12-15B/year in Grad PLUS eliminated.

nodes.title: SEC. 70304 — Extension and Enhancement of Paid Family and Medical Leave Credit
nodes.description: Makes permanent and expands §45S employer credit for paid family and medical leave (removes §45S(i) sunset). Restructures credit as election: (A) applicable percentage of wages paid during leave, OR (B) applicable percentage of insurance premiums paid for qualifying FMLA insurance policy. Insurance premium option: rate of payment does not require employees to actually take leave — credit exists even with zero leave taken. Minimum employment period reduced from 1 year to 6 months (electable). Part-time employees (20+ hours/week customarily) now qualify. Aggregation rule: §414(b)/(c) single employer treatment with exceptions for 'substantial and legitimate business reason' — explicitly cannot cite state/local FMLA law as reason for exception. State/local mandated leave counted toward policy requirement but NOT toward credit amount calculation. §280C(a) no-double-benefit: deduction reduced by credit; new sentence for premium-based credit. Applicable percentage: 12%–25% tiered structure. Effective: tax years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 90006 — Presidential Residence Protection
nodes.description: Appropriates $300,000,000 to the Administrator of FEMA for fiscal year 2025, available until September 30, 2029, for the reimbursement of extraordinary law enforcement personnel costs for protection activities directly and demonstrably associated with any residence of the President designated pursuant to section 3 or 4 of the Presidential Protection Assistance Act of 1976 (Pub. L. 94-524; 18 U.S.C. 3056 note) to be secured by the United States Secret Service. AVAILABILITY (subsec. b): Funds available only for costs that a State or local agency (1) incurred or incurs on or after July 1, 2024; (2) demonstrates as being (A) in excess of typical law enforcement operation costs, (B) directly attributable to the provision of protection described in this section, and (C) associated with a nongovernmental property designated pursuant to section 3 or 4 of the Presidential Protection Assistance Act of 1976 to be secured by the Secret Service; and (3) certifies as compensating protection activities requested by the United States Secret Service. FEMA may use not more than 3 percent for administering grants.

nodes.title: SEC. 40006 — Corporate Average Fuel Economy Civil Penalties
nodes.description: Eliminates all CAFE civil penalties. Amends 49 USC 32912. Bill text: 'Section 32912 of title 49, United States Code, is amended — (1) in subsection (b), in the matter preceding paragraph (1), by striking "$5" and inserting "$0.00"; and (2) in subsection (c)(1)(B), by striking "$10" and inserting "$0.00".' Prior law: $5 per 1/10 mpg below standard per vehicle (passenger cars); $10 per 1/10 mpg (non-passenger/light trucks). Effective on enactment. Retroactivity clause: 'apply to all model years of a manufacturer for which the Secretary of Transportation has not provided a notification pursuant to section 32903(b)(2)(B) of title 49.' CAFE standards themselves (49 USC 32902) remain in force — creates unenforceable standards with zero financial consequence. Pending NHTSA penalty assessments (Mercedes, BMW, Porsche, Stellantis, Volvo, Ferrari) retroactively eliminated. No reinstatement mechanism, no inflation adjustment — permanent zero penalty.

nodes.title: SEC. 71301 — Permitting Premium Tax Credit Only for Certain Individuals
nodes.description: Section 36B(e)(1) is amended by inserting 'or, in the case of aliens who are lawfully present, are not eligible aliens' after 'individuals who are not lawfully present'. ELIGIBLE ALIENS defined in new subparagraph (B): An individual who is an alien and lawfully present shall be treated as an eligible alien if such individual is, and is reasonably expected to be for the entire period of enrollment—(i) an alien who is lawfully admitted for permanent residence under the Immigration and Nationality Act (8 U.S.C. 1101 et seq.), (ii) an alien who has been granted the status of Cuban and Haitian entrant, as defined in section 501(e) of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980 (Public Law 96–422); or (iii) an individual who lawfully resides in the United States in accordance with a Compact of Free Association referred to in section 402(b)(2)(G) of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996. CONFORMING AMENDMENTS to ACA Sections 1411 and 1412 add immigration status verification. Section 5000A(d)(3) amended to substitute 'eligible alien (within the meaning of section 36B(e)(2))' for 'alien lawfully present.' EFFECTIVE DATE: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026 (ACA conforming amendments: plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2027). [Lines 14351–14428]

nodes.title: SEC. 60010 — Rescission of Funding for Greenhouse Gas Corporate Reporting
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60111 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2072) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for EPA's mandatory greenhouse gas corporate reporting program (GHGRP), which requires large emitters to report GHG emissions annually under 40 C.F.R. Part 98. IRA appropriated $5 million under Sec. 60111. The underlying GHGRP regulatory requirement is NOT repealed, but its funding is removed. BURIED PROVISION: Defunding a reporting mandate without repealing it creates compliance ambiguity. Effective on enactment. Losers: EPA's GHGRP data collection capacity; investors and researchers relying on corporate emissions data.

nodes.title: Mixed-status household double penalty in SEC. 10108
nodes.description: The income-counting provision at the end of the new §6(f) text creates a compounding effect for mixed-status households: the ineligible non-citizen household member is excluded from the benefit unit (reducing household size for allotment calculation) BUT their income is still counted against the eligible members' benefit calculation. This penalizes the household twice. The provision reads: 'The income (less, at State option, a pro rata share) and financial resources of the individual rendered ineligible to participate in the supplemental nutrition assistance program under this subsection shall be considered in determining the eligibility and the value of the allotment of the household of which such individual is a member.' Cross-reference: this provision interacts with SEC. 10102 (work requirements) and SEC. 10105 (state cost-sharing) to compound impacts on vulnerable immigrant families.

nodes.title: SEC. 50204 — Authorization to Mine Federal Coal
nodes.description: 'Federal coal reserves located in Federal land subject to a mining plan previously approved by the Secretary of the Interior as of the date of enactment of this Act and adjacent to coal reserves in adjacent State or private land are authorized to be mined.' Requirement: 'Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary of the Interior shall, without substantial modification, take such steps as are necessary to authorize the mining of Federal land described in subsection (a).' NEPA carve-out: 'Nothing in this section shall prevent a review under the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.).' — nominally preserves NEPA but 90-day mandatory authorization makes meaningful review impossible. Bypasses competitive leasing and potentially fair market value requirements. Allows expansion of existing private mining operations onto adjacent public lands without new competitive bidding.

nodes.title: SEC. 90007 — DHS Appropriations for Border Support
nodes.description: Appropriates $10,000,000,000 to the Secretary of Homeland Security for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for reimbursement of costs incurred in undertaking activities in support of the Department of Homeland Security's mission to safeguard the borders of the United States. No enumerated permitted uses, no reporting requirements, no spend plan requirements. Appropriation is to the Secretary directly — not a named component agency — giving maximum discretion. Reimbursement framing could flow to DHS components or to other federal agencies such as DOD that provided border support under military-civilian cooperation agreements.

nodes.title: SEC. 30004 — B DPA appropriation gives executive near-total discretion over industrial policy funds
nodes.description: ,000,000,000 appropriated to carry out the Defense Production Act (50 U.S.C. 4501 et seq.), available FY2025 through September 30, 2027. 'Congress provides no further direction in this section on which industries or programs must receive funding, leaving allocation entirely to the executive.' DPA authority includes: prioritizing contracts, making loans, purchasing and selling strategic materials, and expanding productive capacity. No restrictions on which supply chains or sectors receive the funds. Potential beneficiaries include semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, rare earth minerals. Foreign suppliers may be displaced by domestic sourcing mandates funded through this appropriation. The title as a whole appropriates B while simultaneously constraining two regulators (CFPB, SEC) and rescinding an unspecified amount of housing funds — net fiscal effect on Treasury is likely positive aside from this new appropriation.

nodes.title: SEC. 71106 — Payment Reduction for Erroneous Excess Payments Under Medicaid
nodes.description: Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396b(u)(1). Key changes: (1) 'Erroneous excess payments' now explicitly include 'payments where insufficient information is available to confirm eligibility' (not just confirmed ineligibility) — adds new subclause (III) to §1903(u)(1)(D)(i); (2) Secretary may now conduct audits directly, or at Secretary's option audits conducted by State (previously state-conducted only); (3) Cap on waiver of payment reductions clarified — cannot exceed amount by which error payments exceed 0.03 allowable rate; (4) New subclause (III) added: payments to individuals not eligible, or where eligibility cannot be confirmed. Effective beginning fiscal year 2030. Transform system that penalized confirmed ineligibility into one that penalizes any evidentiary gap — states will respond by demanding more documentation from enrollees. Individuals eligible but unable to produce documentation (rural, homeless, limited English proficiency) face more scrutiny.

nodes.title: SEC. 60011 — Rescission of Funding for Environmental Product Declaration Assistance
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60112 of Public Law 117-169 (42 U.S.C. 4321 note; 136 Stat. 2072) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for EPA's program assisting manufacturers in developing Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) — life-cycle carbon accounting documents for construction materials (steel, cement, glass). IRA appropriated $250 million under Sec. 60112. NOTE: The NEPA citation (42 U.S.C. 4321) in the statutory reference signals the EPD program was anchored partly to NEPA environmental assessment authority. Effective on enactment. Losers: domestic manufacturers investing in low-carbon production, federal procurement programs using EPDs. Beneficiaries: high-carbon material producers.

nodes.title: SEC. 20008 — Enhancement of Resources for Nuclear Forces
nodes.description: Appropriates approximately $14.688 billion total ($10.803B DoD + $3.885B NNSA) for nuclear triad modernization. Bill text (lines 2887-2955). DoD Subsection (a): $2,500,000,000 'for risk reduction activities for the Sentinel intercontinental ballistic missile program'; $4,500,000,000 'only for expansion of production capacity of B-21 long-range bomber aircraft and the purchase of aircraft only available through the expansion of production capacity'; $500,000,000 'for improvements to the Minuteman III intercontinental ballistic missile system'; $2,000,000,000 'to accelerate the development, procurement, and integration of the nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile'; $62,000,000 'to convert Ohio-class submarine tubes to accept additional missiles, not to be obligated before March 1, 2026'; $400,000,000 'to accelerate the development of Trident D5LE2 submarine-launched ballistic missiles'; $168,000,000 'to accelerate the production of the Survivable Airborne Operations Center program'. NNSA Subsection (b): $1,000,000,000 'to accelerate the construction of National Nuclear Security Administration facilities pursuant to section 3211 of the National Nuclear Security Administration Act (50 U.S.C. 2401)'; $400,000,000 'to accelerate the development, procurement, and integration of the warhead for the nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile'; $750,000,000 each for primary and secondary capability modernization; $120,000,000 'to accelerate domestic uranium enrichment centrifuge deployment for defense purposes'; $10,000,000 'for National Nuclear Security Administration evaluation of spent fuel reprocessing technology' — civilian spent fuel reprocessing has been banned since Carter 1977 on nonproliferation grounds; framing as 'defense purposes' is a policy workaround. The SLCM-N restoration ($2.4B combined) represents major arms control policy reversal — canceled under Obama. Ohio-class tube conversion not obligatable before March 1, 2026.

nodes.title: SEC. 71302 — Disallowing Premium Tax Credit During Periods of Medicaid Ineligibility Due to Alien Status
nodes.description: Section 36B(c)(1) is amended by striking subparagraph (B). That subparagraph had treated certain aliens ineligible for Medicaid due to their immigration status as if they met the minimum essential coverage eligibility requirement for purposes of PTC qualification. EFFECTIVE DATE: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025 — one year earlier than the main SEC. 71301 restriction. [Lines 14429–14436]

nodes.title: SNAP Subtitle A: compounding cuts to low-income households
nodes.description: The six Subtitle A SNAP provisions work in concert to substantially reduce SNAP enrollment and benefit levels: (1) TFP lock (10101) prevents future benefit increases beyond CPI; (2) work requirement expansion to age 64 (10102) removes ~1M adults from eligibility; (3) SUA restriction (10103) reduces shelter deductions for non-elderly/disabled; (4) internet expense exclusion (10104) further reduces shelter deductions; (5) state benefit cost-sharing up to 15% (10105) incentivizes state caseload reduction; (6) admin cost-sharing cut from 50% to 25% (10106) reduces state capacity to administer program. States facing FY2028 benefit cost-shares of 10-15% have a structural incentive to reduce caseloads by tightening eligibility determinations, which compounds work requirement effects. Budget analysts estimate these provisions together could remove 3-5 million households from SNAP over 5 years.

nodes.title: SEC. 100004 — IMMIGRATION PAROLE FEE (8 U.S.C. 1804)
nodes.description: Mandatory non-waivable $1,000 fee on every alien paroled into the United States under INA § 212(d)(5). Verbatim (lines 16973-17064): 'the Secretary of Homeland Security shall require the payment of a fee, equal to the amount specified in this section and in addition to any other fee authorized by law, by any alien who is paroled into the United States.' INITIAL: greater of $1,000 or higher by rule. CPI-indexed annually rounded to next lowest $10. DISPOSITION: 'All of the fees collected pursuant to this section shall be deposited into the general fund of the Treasury.' — 100% Treasury. Exceptions (b)(1)-(10): medical emergency with no treatment available abroad OR life-threatening; parent/guardian of that minor; organ/tissue donor with no time; close family member with imminent death; funeral attendance if timing impossible; adopted child urgent medical; AOS applicant returning from travel; alien returned to contiguous country for hearing; Cuban/Haitian entrant; law enforcement cooperator with Secretary individualized 'significant public benefit' determination. NO FEE WAIVER except specific exceptions. All non-exception parole revenue to general Treasury. Cross-refs: INA § 212(d)(5) (8 U.S.C. 1182(d)(5)); § 235(b)(2)(C); REAA § 501(e).

nodes.title: SEC. 40007 — Payments for Lease of Metropolitan Washington Airports
nodes.description: Rewrites 49 USC 49104(b) to increase MWAA annual lease payment for Reagan National (DCA) and Dulles airports. Bill text replaces prior $3,000,000/yr (1987 dollars) with: '(A) during the period from 1987 to 2026, equal to $3,000,000 in 1987 dollars; and (B) for 2027 and subsequent years, equal to $15,000,000 in 2027 dollars.' Renegotiation clause: 'The Secretary and the Airports Authority shall renegotiate the level of lease payments at least once every 10 years to ensure that in no year the amount specified in paragraph (1)(B) is less than $15,000,000 in 2027 dollars.' One-way ratchet: renegotiation can only go up, not down. Prior real-dollar equivalent ~$8-9M (2025); new floor $15M — roughly 5x real-dollar increase. GNP Price Deflator indexing applies.

nodes.title: SEC. 70506 — Termination of Residential Clean Energy Credit
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 25D(h) striking 'to property placed in service after December 31, 2034' and inserting 'with respect to any expenditures made after December 31, 2025'. Terminates 30% residential solar, wind, geothermal, battery storage, and fuel cell tax credit. Was originally slated to run through 2034 with step-down to 26% in 2033 and 22% in 2034. Conforming amendments to § 25D(g): paragraph (2) inserts 'and' after comma; paragraph (3) strikes 'and before January 1, 2033, 30 percent,' inserting '30 percent.'; strikes paragraphs (4) and (5) (the 2033/2034 phase-down rates). Enacted by IRA 2022 § 13302. CBO ~$5B/year; terminating 9 years early = ~$45 billion in forgone expenditure. Credit also covers standalone home battery storage (not paired with solar). All expenditures must be made by December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 50301 — Timber Sales and Long-Term Contracting (Forest Service and BLM)
nodes.description: Forest Service: 'For each of fiscal years 2026 through 2034, the Secretary shall sell timber annually on National Forest System land in a total quantity that is not less than 250,000,000 board-feet greater than the quantity of board-feet sold in the previous fiscal year.' Capped at allowable sale quantity under forest plan in effect at enactment. Long-term contracts: 'not fewer than 40 long-term timber sale contracts' for FY2025-2034, 'period... shall be not less than 20 years, with options for extensions or renewals.' BLM: 'not less than 20,000,000 board-feet greater than the quantity of board-feet sold in the previous fiscal year' each FY2026-2034; 'not fewer than 5 long-term contracts' of minimum 20 years. 'Any monies derived from a timber sale contract... shall be deposited in the general fund of the Treasury.' Compounding ratchet structure: each year's floor = prior year's actual sales + 250M board-feet — no off-ramp for fire/pest damage or market collapse. 20-year contracts lock in cutting rights well beyond any single administration.

nodes.title: SEC. 90101 — FEHB Improvements (FEHB Protection Act of 2025)
nodes.description: Short title: FEHB Protection Act of 2025 (5 U.S.C. 8905 note). Requires OPM Director to: (c) VERIFICATION REQUIREMENTS — not later than 1 year after enactment, issue regulations and implement a process to verify (1) the veracity of any qualifying life event through which an enrollee seeks to add a member of family and (2) that any individual so added is a qualifying member of family, including during any open season. (d) FRAUD RISK ASSESSMENT — in any fraud risk assessment conducted on or after enactment, Director shall include assessment of individuals enrolled even though not eligible to be enrolled. (e) FAMILY MEMBER ELIGIBILITY VERIFICATION AUDIT — during the 3-year period beginning 1 year after enactment, Director shall carry out a comprehensive audit regarding members of family covered under the Program, reviewing marriage certificates, birth certificates, and other appropriate documents to determine eligibility. (f) DISENROLLMENT OR REMOVAL — not later than 180 days after enactment, Director shall develop a process to disenroll or remove individuals not eligible for enrollment. FUNDING: Amends 5 U.S.C. 8909 to insert new paragraph (b)(2): In fiscal year 2026, $66,000,000 to be derived from all contributions, to remain available until end of fiscal year 2035. The $66M set-aside is explicitly exempted from the limitations that may be specified annually by Congress — bypassing normal congressional oversight of FEHB administrative spending.

nodes.title: SEC. 82001 / Subtitle C — Loan Repayment: Creates RAP, Eliminates SAVE/PAYE/ICR
nodes.description: Most complex section. Adds new §455(q) to HEA. (1) ELIMINATES income contingent repayment: 'Subsection (e) of section 455 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1087e(e)) is repealed' effective July 1, 2028. All ICR/SAVE/PAYE borrowers must transition by July 1, 2028; if they fail to select, 'the Secretary of Education shall enroll the covered income contingent loans of such borrower in the Repayment Assistance Plan.' (2) NEW STANDARD PLAN for loans made on/after July 1, 2026 — tiered by total outstanding principal: under $25,000 = 10 years; $25,000-$50,000 = 15 years; $50,000-$100,000 = 20 years; $100,000+ = 25 years. (3) REPAYMENT ASSISTANCE PLAN (RAP) — new income-based plan with progressive payment schedule: AGI ≤$10,000 = $120/year flat; $10K-$20K = 1% AGI; $20K-$30K = 2%; $30K-$40K = 3%; $40K-$50K = 4%; $50K-$60K = 5%; $60K-$70K = 6%; $70K-$80K = 7%; $80K-$90K = 8%; $90K-$100K = 9%; over $100K = 10%. Monthly payment = (applicable base payment / 12) minus '$50 for each dependent.' Minimum: '$10.' (4) FORGIVENESS: 'The Secretary shall cancel any outstanding balance...who has made 360 qualifying monthly payments.' (5) INTEREST SUBSIDY: unpaid monthly interest 'shall not be charged to the borrower.' (6) PRINCIPAL MATCHING: if monthly payment reduces principal by less than $50, 'the Secretary shall reduce such total outstanding principal balance of the borrower by an amount equal to [the lesser of $50 or total paid] minus [amount applied to principal].' (7) NONCOMPLIANCE: borrowers who fail to provide income docs default to 10-year standard plan payment. (8) PARENT PLUS loans are 'excepted loans' ineligible for RAP. (9) Married filing separately: spouse income excluded from AGI for RAP. Automatic IRS recertification via §6103(l)(13).

nodes.title: SEC. 60012 — Rescission of Funding for Methane Emissions and Waste Reduction Incentive Program; Extension of Compliance Period
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: '(a) RESCISSION.—The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out subsections (a) and (b) of section 136 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7436) are rescinded. (b) PERIOD.—Section 136(g) of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7436(g)) is amended by striking ''calendar year 2024'' and inserting ''calendar year 2034''.' Analysis: TWO-PART section — (a) rescinds unobligated balances of the methane fee program (IRA appropriated $850 million); (b) STATUTORY AMENDMENT extending compliance period by 10 years. MOST CONSEQUENTIAL SECTION in Title VI beyond GGRF repeal. The statutory amendment to Sec. 136(g) is a substantive policy change buried alongside a rescission. EPA cannot charge methane waste emission fees until after calendar year 2034 — a full decade's reprieve worth potentially billions in avoided fees to oil and gas operators. The methane waste emissions charge was the IRA's primary enforcement mechanism against oil and gas methane leaks. Losers: communities near oil/gas operations; climate goals; Treasury foregone revenue.

nodes.title: SEC. 71107 — Eligibility Redeterminations Every 6 Months for ACA Expansion Adults
nodes.description: Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(14) by adding new subparagraph (L). For redeterminations scheduled on or after the first day of the first quarter that begins after December 31, 2026 (i.e., January 1, 2027): states shall make redeterminations once every 6 months (previously 12 months) for: (I) Individuals enrolled under §1902(a)(10)(A)(i)(VIII) — ACA expansion adults ages 19–64, income up to 138% FPL; (II) Individuals in equivalent minimum essential coverage waivers. Exemption: individuals described in subsection (xx)(9)(A)(ii)(II) — 'specified excluded individuals' under work requirement provisions (medically frail, pregnant, parents of children under 13, veterans with total disability, Indians, etc.). HHS must issue guidance within 180 days of enactment. ,000,000 appropriated to CMS for FY2026 implementation. ~21 million ACA expansion enrollees subject. Post-COVID unwinding data: ~20–30% of people disenrolled during redeterminations were later re-enrolled as eligible. Doubling frequency = millions of person-months of wrongful coverage gaps annually.

nodes.title: SEC. 70305 — Exceptions from Limitations on Deduction for Business Meals
nodes.description: Creates two new exceptions to business meal deduction limitations. (1) Amends §274(o): restores full deductibility for employer-provided meals meeting §274(e)(8) exceptions. (2) New §274(n)(2)(C)(v): 100% deductible meals provided on fishing vessels, fish processing vessels, or fish tender vessels (46 U.S.C. §2101), OR at fish processing facilities north of 50 degrees north latitude and not in a metropolitan statistical area (§143(k)(2)(B)). Targets remote Alaska fishing/processing operations in Bering Sea and Gulf of Alaska. Effective: amounts paid or incurred after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 10201 — Rescission of Amounts for Forestry
nodes.description: Rescinds all unobligated balances from four IRA (Public Law 117-169) forestry appropriations. Exact text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts appropriated by the following provisions of Public Law 117-169 are rescinded: (1) Paragraphs (3) and (4) of section 23001(a) (136 Stat. 2023). (2) Paragraphs (1) through (4) of section 23002(a) (136 Stat. 2025). (3) Section 23003(a)(2) (136 Stat. 2026). (4) Section 23005 (136 Stat. 2027).' IRA had appropriated ~.15B total for Forest Service reforestation, hazardous fuels reduction, watershed restoration, legacy roads/trails, and urban/community forestry. Only unobligated balances are rescinded — already-committed funds are retained. Effective on enactment. Cross-reference: SEC. 10601(g) rescinds parallel IRA conservation funds.

nodes.title: SEC. 70507 — Termination of Energy Efficient Commercial Buildings Deduction
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 179D by adding new subsection (i): 'TERMINATION.—This section shall not apply with respect to property the construction of which begins after June 30, 2026.' Enhanced deduction for energy-efficient commercial building improvements (up to $5.65/sq ft under IRA expansion). Enacted by IRA 2022 § 13303. CBO ~$2 billion/year. Construction must begin by June 30, 2026 to qualify — 'begins construction' trigger rather than placed-in-service is consequential: projects already permitted/designed can proceed, but planning-stage projects face tight deadline. Loses: building owners, A/E firms specializing in energy efficiency, HVAC and lighting system manufacturers, commercial energy consultants.

nodes.title: SEC. 71303 — Requiring Verification of Eligibility for Premium Tax Credit
nodes.description: Section 36B(c) is amended by adding new paragraphs: (5) EXCHANGE ENROLLMENT VERIFICATION REQUIREMENT: The term 'coverage month' shall not include any month beginning before the Exchange verifies, using applicable enrollment information that shall be provided or verified by the applicant, such individual's eligibility—(i) to enroll in the plan through the Exchange, and (ii) for any advance payment under section 1412 of the ACA. Applicable enrollment information shall include: (i) Household income and family size. (ii) Whether the individual is an eligible alien. (iii) Any health coverage status or eligibility for coverage. (iv) Place of residence. (v) Such other information as may be determined by the Secretary. Waiver available for special enrollment periods triggered by family size changes. (6) EXCHANGE COMPLIANCE WITH FILING REQUIREMENTS: The term 'coverage month' shall not include any month for which the Exchange does not meet the requirements of section 155.305(f)(4)(iii) of title 45, Code of Federal Regulations (as published in the Federal Register on June 25, 2025 (90 Fed. Reg. 27074), applied as though it applied to all plan years after 2025). PRE-ENROLLMENT VERIFICATION PROCESS REQUIRED: beginning not later than August 1, verify with the Exchange the applicant's household income and eligibility for enrollment for plan years beginning in the subsequent year. EFFECTIVE DATE: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2027. [Lines 14438–14520]

nodes.title: SEC. 40008 — Rescission of Certain Amounts for NOAA
nodes.description: Rescinds all unobligated balances from four IRA NOAA programs. Bill text: 'Any unobligated balances of amounts appropriated or otherwise made available by sections 40001, 40002, 40003, and 40004 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2028) are hereby rescinded.' IRA (P.L. 117-169) NOAA sections covered: 40001 (fisheries/coastal habitat restoration), 40002 (climate-resilient coast grants), 40003 (weather forecasting improvements), 40004 (regional ocean partnership programs). Original IRA appropriation to NOAA under these sections: approximately $3.655 billion total. Rescinded amount = all unobligated balances at enactment. Effective immediately. No amendment to underlying statute — cancels unspent spending authority only.

nodes.title: SEC. 20009 — Enhancement of DoD Resources for INDOPACOM Capabilities
nodes.description: Appropriates approximately $12.1 billion for INDOPACOM-specific capabilities, offensive cyber, space assets, and economic warfare. Bill text (lines 2960-3029): 'In addition to amounts otherwise available, there are appropriated to the Secretary of Defense for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029.' Key line items: $3,650,000,000 'for the development, procurement, and integration of United States military satellites and the protection of United States military satellites'; $1,100,000,000 'for development of infrastructure within the area of operations of United States Indo-Pacific Command'; $1,000,000,000 'for offensive cyber operations' (unusually direct language for classified activities); $1,000,000,000 'for the X-37B military spacecraft program'; $532,600,000 'for the Pacific Air Force biennial large-scale exercise'; $528,000,000 'for DARC and SILENTBARKER military space situational awareness programs'; $500,000,000 'for the development, coordination, and deployment of economic competition effects within the Department of Defense' (authorizes DoD economic warfare — commercial pressure and disruption activities within a military command); $450,000,000 'for the development of airfields within the area of operations of United States Indo-Pacific Command'; $850,000,000 'for the replenishment of military articles'; $350,000,000 'for the development, procurement, and integration of military space command and control systems'; $300,000,000 'for the procurement of mesh network communications capabilities for Special Operations Command Pacific'; $200,000,000 'for acceleration of Guam Defense System program'; $115,000,000 'for exploration and development of existing Arctic infrastructure' (Arctic is NORTHCOM/EUCOM territory — geographic mismatch); $30,000,000 'for surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities for United States Africa Command'. All funds through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 100005 — SPECIAL IMMIGRANT JUVENILE FEE (8 U.S.C. 1805)
nodes.description: New $250 minimum fee on applications for Special Immigrant Juvenile (SIJ) status under INA § 101(a)(27)(J) (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(27)(J)). Verbatim (lines 17065-17093): 'the Secretary of Homeland Security shall require the payment of a fee, equal to the amount specified in this section, by any alien, parent, or legal guardian of an alien applying for special immigrant juvenile status under section 101(a)(27)(J) (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(27)(J)).' INITIAL: greater of $250 or higher by rule. CPI-indexed annually. DISPOSITION: 'All of the fees collected pursuant to this section shall be deposited into the general fund of the Treasury.' — 100% Treasury. NOTABLE DRAFTING ANOMALY: Section contains NO 'No Fee Waiver' subsection — every other section in Part I has explicit § (X)(e) 'No Fee Waiver'. This may be inadvertent omission creating ambiguity about waiver availability. SIJ applicants are abused, neglected, or abandoned immigrant children in state court dependency proceedings — by definition indigent minors. Cross-refs: INA § 101(a)(27)(J) (8 U.S.C. 1101(a)(27)(J)). Effective FY2025, CPI adjustments FY2026.

nodes.title: SEC. 60013 — Rescission of Funding for Greenhouse Gas Air Pollution Plans and Implementation Grants
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 137 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7437) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for state and local grants to develop and implement greenhouse gas air pollution reduction plans under CAA Sec. 137 (42 U.S.C. 7437). IRA appropriated $5 billion under Sec. 60114 — one of the larger dollar-figure rescissions in the title. Program statute is NOT repealed. Effective on enactment. Losers: state and local governments that had applied for or were anticipating these grants to fund GHG reduction planning.

nodes.title: SEC. 90102 — Pandemic Response Accountability Committee
nodes.description: Appropriates $88,000,000 for fiscal year 2026, to remain available until expended, to the Pandemic Response Accountability Committee to support oversight of the Coronavirus response and of funds provided in this Act or any other Act pertaining to the Coronavirus pandemic. Amends CARES Act Section 15010 (5 U.S.C. 424 note; Pub. L. 116-136; 134 Stat. 533): (1) in subsection (a)(6), adds subparagraph (G) to covered legislation — 'the Act titled An Act to provide for reconciliation pursuant to title II of H. Con. Res. 14'; (2) in subsection (k), strikes '2025' and inserts '2034' — extending the PRAC sunset by 9 years. PRAC will thus have oversight authority over immigration enforcement spending, border wall contracts, and all other Title IX appropriations through 2034.

nodes.title: SEC. 50302 — Renewable Energy Fees on Federal Land
nodes.description: Establishes mandatory fee structure for wind/solar on federal land. Acreage rent formula: 'Acreage rent = A × B × ((1 + C)^D)' where A=Per-Acre Rate (5-yr average pastureland rental rates), B=Encumbrance Factor (100% solar; ≥10% wind), C=Annual Adjustment Factor (3%), D=year in right-of-way term. Capacity fee: 'annually collect a capacity fee... equal to the greater of (A) an amount equal to the acreage rent... and (B) 3.9 percent of the gross proceeds from the sale of electricity produced by the renewable energy project.' Wind multi-use reduction: 10% reduction available only if '≥25 percent of the land within the area of the right-of-way is authorized for use... with respect to an activity other than the generation of wind energy for the entirety of the year.' Late payment: fee after 15 days; 'The Secretary may terminate a right-of-way for a renewable energy project if the Secretary does not receive payment... by the date that is 90 days after the date on which the payment was due.' Critical asymmetry: 3.9% gross revenue fee on renewables vs. 12.5% royalty on extracted fossil fuel value — normalized for energy output, renewables face more aggressive take rate. No comparable fee imposed on new fossil fuel development.

nodes.title: SEC. 70508 — Termination of New Energy Efficient Home Credit
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 45L(h) striking 'December 31, 2032' and inserting 'June 30, 2026'. Terminates credit for homebuilders constructing energy-efficient new homes (up to $5,000 per qualifying home). Enacted by IRA 2022 § 13304. CBO ~$1.5-2 billion/year. Homes must be acquired by June 30, 2026. Homebuilders need to account for construction timelines — homes being built now that will be sold after June 30, 2026 may lose eligibility. Loses: DR Horton, Lennar, PulteGroup and other large homebuilders who had incorporated the credit into their business model.

nodes.title: SEC. 70306 — Increased Dollar Limitations for Expensing of Certain Depreciable Business Assets
nodes.description: Raises §179 immediate expensing cap from $1,000,000 to $2,500,000 and phaseout threshold from $2,500,000 to $4,000,000. §179(b)(6)(A) inflation adjustment updated: new dollar amounts indexed from calendar year 2024 (vs. 2017 for the $500 small vehicle cap). Combined with 100% bonus depreciation from §70301, creates complete first-year write-off for all business property. Phaseout is dollar-for-dollar above $4M threshold: businesses can acquire up to $6.5M of §179 property before losing benefit entirely. Effective: property placed in service in taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.

nodes.title: SEC. 90103 — Appropriation for the Office of Management and Budget
nodes.description: Appropriates $100,000,000 to the Office of Management and Budget for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029, for purposes of finding budget and accounting efficiencies in the executive branch. Single-sentence authorization. No enumerated uses beyond 'efficiencies.' No reporting requirements to Congress. No restrictions on how funds are spent. OMB is the agency that oversees all other agencies' budgets — creating a circular dynamic where OMB funds its own oversight of others. Closest explicit DOGE-adjacent appropriation in the bill.

nodes.title: SEC. 71108 — Revising Home Equity Limit for Long-Term Care Medicaid Eligibility
nodes.description: Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396p(f)(1) and 42 U.S.C. 1396a(r)(2), (e)(14)(D)(iv). Changes: (1) States may elect, without regard to statewideness (§1902(a)(1)) and comparability (§1902(a)(10)(B)) requirements, to apply the home equity limit at an amount exceeding the §1917(f)(1)(A) amount but not exceeding ,000,000 for non-agricultural homes; (2) Agricultural home limit (homes on lots zoned for agricultural use) unchanged from current inflation-adjusted amount — no M cap applies; (3) Inflation adjustment cap: for non-agricultural homes, cap held at ,000,000 — if inflation adjustment would exceed M, amount deemed to be ,000,000; (4) Critical clarification (§1902(r)(2)(C)): 'This paragraph shall not be construed as permitting a State to determine the eligibility of an individual for medical assistance with respect to nursing facility services or other long-term care services without application of the limit under section 1917(f)(1).' Also amends §1902(e)(14)(D)(iv) to add: 'Section 1917(f) shall apply for purposes of determining the eligibility of an individual for medical assistance with respect to nursing facility services or other long-term care services.' Effective January 1, 2028. Closes MAGI loophole for LTC Medicaid.

nodes.title: SEC. 10301 — Effective Reference Price; Reference Price
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 9011. Two changes: (1) Raises effective reference price trigger from 85% to 88% of Olympic moving average (strikes '85' and inserts 'beginning with the crop year 2025, 88'). (2) Replaces paragraph (19) reference price definition with new prices effective 2025 crop year: wheat .35/bu, corn .10/bu, grain sorghum .40/bu, barley .45/bu, oats .65/bu, long grain rice .90/cwt, medium grain rice .90/cwt, soybeans .00/bu, other oilseeds .75/cwt, peanuts .00/ton, dry peas .10/cwt, lentils .75/cwt, small chickpeas .65/cwt, large chickpeas .65/cwt, seed cotton /bin/zsh.42/lb. Beginning 2031 crop year: reference price for prior year multiplied by 1.005 annually. Cap: 'In no case shall a reference price for a covered commodity exceed 113 percent of the reference price for such covered commodity listed in subparagraph (A).' Prior prices: wheat .50, corn .70, soybeans .40, peanuts /ton, seed cotton /bin/zsh.367/lb. Increases range from ~10-18% across crops.

nodes.title: SEC. 60014 — Rescission of Funding for EPA Efficient, Accurate, and Timely Reviews
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60115 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2077) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds provided specifically to improve EPA's speed and accuracy in conducting environmental reviews under NEPA. IRA appropriated $100 million under Sec. 60115. IRONY: This funding was meant to speed reviews, and it is rescinded in the same title that adds a pay-for-speed NEPA option (Sec. 60026). PATTERN: Rescission of review-speed funding, paired with creation of a fee-based speed mechanism in Sec. 60026, shifts the cost of faster reviews from EPA's budget to project sponsors — effectively privatizing environmental review speed. See also Sec. 60023. Effective on enactment.

nodes.title: SEC. 40009 — Reduction in Annual Transfers to Travel Promotion Fund
nodes.description: Reduces annual mandatory ESTA fee transfer to Travel Promotion Fund from $100 million to $20 million (80% cut). Amends Travel Promotion Act of 2009, 22 USC 2131(d)(2)(B). Bill text: 'Subsection (d)(2)(B) of the Travel Promotion Act of 2009 (22 U.S.C. 2131(d)(2)(B)) is amended by striking "$100,000,000" and inserting "$20,000,000".' Travel Promotion Fund finances Brand USA — the public-private partnership marketing the U.S. as a destination to international travelers. $80 million/yr reduction diverted to general Treasury. Effective upon enactment. Brand USA's operating model requires hundreds of millions annually; $20M effectively defunds the program while technically preserving it.

nodes.title: SEC. 82002 — Deferment; Forbearance: Eliminate Unemployment/Hardship Deferments, Cap Forbearance
nodes.description: Amends HEA §455(f) (20 U.S.C. 1087e(f)). For loans originated on or after July 1, 2027: 'A borrower who receives a loan made under this part on or after July 1, 2027, shall not be eligible to defer such loan under subparagraph (B) or (D) of paragraph (2)' — eliminating unemployment deferment (up to 3 years) and economic hardship deferment (up to 3 years). Forbearance cap: 'A borrower who receives a loan made under this part on or after July 1, 2027, may only be eligible for a forbearance on such loan pursuant to section 428(c)(3)(B) that does not exceed 9 months during any 24-month period.' Only safety valve for job loss is RAP minimum $10/month payment. Effective July 1, 2027 for new borrowers.

nodes.title: SEC. 71303: Lock-in of 45 C.F.R. 155.305(f)(4)(iii) published June 25, 2025 (9 days before enactment) — regulatory version frozen in statute, future administrations cannot change without Act of Congress
nodes.description: The Exchange compliance requirement in paragraph (6) ties to a specific CFR citation 'as published in the Federal Register on June 25, 2025 (90 Fed. Reg. 27074), applied as though it applied to all plan years after 2025.' This lock-in of a specific regulatory version is unusual. Additionally, Exchanges that fail to comply with this reporting requirement lose their qualified health plan designation — potentially disrupting coverage for ALL enrolled in non-compliant Exchanges, not just individual violators.

nodes.title: Cross-title IRA rollback pattern: SEC. 30002 (Title III) is one of at least 12 IRA rescission provisions across Titles I, III, VI, and VII
nodes.description: SEC. 30002 (Title III) rescinds unobligated GRRP housing retrofit funds (IRA P.L. 117-169, ~.5M original appropriation). This is part of a systematic multi-title pattern of IRA rescissions and terminations throughout the bill: Title I — SEC. 10201 rescinds IRA forestry amounts; Title III — SEC. 30002 rescinds GRRP housing retrofit funds (P.L. 117-169, sec. 30002(a)); Title VI — SEC. 60001 rescinds Clean Heavy-Duty Vehicles funding; SEC. 60002 repeals the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund; SEC. 60003 rescinds Diesel Emissions Reductions funding; SEC. 60004 rescinds air pollution funding; SEC. 60005 rescinds air pollution at schools funding; SEC. 60006 rescinds Low Emissions Electricity Program funding; SEC. 60007 rescinds Sec. 211(o) Clean Air Act funding; SEC. 60008 rescinds American Innovation and Manufacturing Act funding; SEC. 60009 rescinds enforcement technology/public information funding; SEC. 60010 rescinds greenhouse gas corporate reporting funding; SEC. 60011 rescinds methane emissions incentive program funding; SEC. 60012 (and extension); Title VII — SEC. 70501-70507 terminate multiple clean energy tax credits (EVs, home efficiency, commercial buildings, residential clean energy, alt fuel refueling). The analysis notes: 'SEC. 30002 fits a broader pattern visible across multiple titles of this bill: rescinding unobligated IRA green-energy and climate-resilience spending appropriated in 2022.'

nodes.title: SEC. 70509 — Termination of Cost Recovery for Energy Property
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 168(e)(3)(B)(vi), as amended by § 13703 of P.L. 117-169 (IRA), by: (1) striking subclause (I), and (2) redesignating subclauses (II) and (III) as subclauses (I) and (II). Removes the 5-year MACRS accelerated depreciation category for certain energy property that was added by the IRA. Effective date: property the construction of which begins after December 31, 2024 — retroactively applies to construction started in 2025 before enactment. Reduced depreciation acceleration means larger taxable income in early years for energy property investors. Significantly affects tax equity financing structures. Interacts with § 45X, § 45Y, § 48E credit ecosystems.

nodes.title: SEC. 70307 — Special Depreciation Allowance for Qualified Production Property
nodes.description: Creates new IRC §168(n): 100% bonus depreciation for nonresidential real property used as 'integral part of a qualified production activity' (manufacturing, production, or refining of tangible personal property requiring 'substantial transformation'). GROUNDBREAKING: real property ordinarily not eligible for bonus depreciation. Qualified production property requirements: (i) subject to §168; (ii) used as integral part of qualified production; (iii) placed in service in U.S. or possession; (iv) original use commences with taxpayer; (v) construction begins after January 19, 2025 and before January 1, 2029; (vi) designated in election; (vii) placed in service before January 1, 2031. Excluded: offices, admin, lodging, parking, sales, research, software development/engineering, food/beverage sold in same building. Special rule: acquired property not previously used in production during 2021–May 12, 2025 qualifies. Recapture: §1245 recapture applies if property ceases qualifying use within 10 years. Election irrevocable (Secretary consent required). Property treated as §1245 property. AMT: 100% deduction allowed without §56 adjustment. Secretary may extend placed-in-service date for acts of God. Effective: property placed in service after date of enactment.

nodes.title: SEC. 60015 — Rescission of Funding for Low-Embodied Carbon Labeling for Construction Materials
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60116 of Public Law 117-169 (42 U.S.C. 4321 note; 136 Stat. 2077) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for a labeling program identifying low-embodied-carbon construction materials, designed to enable federal procurement preferences for low-carbon steel, concrete, and other materials. IRA appropriated $100 million under Sec. 60116. Note NEPA citation (42 U.S.C. 4321). Effective on enactment. Losers: domestic producers of low-carbon materials who anticipated a federal purchasing advantage; Buy American and clean manufacturing advocates. Beneficiaries: conventional (higher-carbon) material producers.

nodes.title: SEC. 50303 — Renewable Energy Revenue Sharing
nodes.description: 'Beginning on January 1, 2026, the amounts collected from a renewable energy project as bonus bids, rentals, fees, or other payments under a right-of-way, permit, lease, or other authorization shall (A) be deposited in the general fund of the Treasury; and (B) without further appropriation or fiscal year limitation, be allocated as follows: (i) 25 percent shall be paid... to the State within the boundaries of which the revenue is derived. (ii) 25 percent shall be paid... to each county in a State within the boundaries of which the revenue is derived, to be allocated among each applicable county based on the percentage of county land from which the revenue is derived.' Amounts to states/counties 'used in accordance with the requirements of section 35 of the Mineral Leasing Act (30 U.S.C. 191).' County payments 'shall be in addition to a payment in lieu of taxes received by the county under chapter 69 of title 31.' The remaining 50% goes to Treasury general fund — NOT to Land and Water Conservation Fund or conservation accounts. Unlike offshore oil revenues that historically funded LWCF, renewable energy on federal land generates no dedicated conservation benefit.

nodes.title: SEC. 71304 — Disallowing Premium Tax Credit in Case of Certain Coverage Enrolled in During Special Enrollment Period
nodes.description: Section 36B(c)(3)(A), as amended by the preceding provisions of this Act, is amended by adding at the end: '(iii) EXCEPTION IN CASE OF CERTAIN SPECIAL ENROLLMENT PERIODS.—Such term shall not include any plan enrolled in during a special enrollment period provided for by an Exchange—(I) on the basis of the relationship of the individual's expected household income to such a percentage of the poverty line (or such other amount) as is prescribed by the Secretary of Health and Human Services for purposes of such period, and (II) not in connection with the occurrence of an event or change in circumstances specified by the Secretary of Health and Human Services for such purposes.' EFFECTIVE DATE: plan years beginning after December 31, 2025. [Lines 14521–14543]

nodes.title: SEC. 10302 — Base Acres
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 9012. Two changes: (1) extends base acre update provision from 2023 to 2031. (2) Adds new subsection (e) allocating up to 30,000,000 additional base acres. Key text: 'the Secretary shall provide notice to owners of eligible farms pursuant to paragraph (3) and allocate to those eligible farms a total of not more than an additional 30,000,000 base acres in the manner provided in this subsection. An owner of a farm that is eligible to receive an allocation of base acres may elect to not receive that allocation by notifying the Secretary not later than 90 days after receipt of the notice.' Eligibility: farm's 5-year average planted acreage (2019-2023) plus up to 15% of total farm acres in eligible noncovered commodities must exceed existing base acres as of September 30, 2024. Pro-rata reduction if total eligible acres exceed 30M. Effective beginning 2026 crop year. New owner provision at subsection (e)(8): 'the Secretary shall use the planting history of the prior owner or owners of that farm for purposes of determining— (A) eligibility under paragraph (3); (B) eligible acres under paragraph (4); and (C) the allocation of acres under paragraph (5).' — base acre value transfers with land sale.

nodes.title: SEC. 40010 — Treatment of Unobligated Funds for Alternative Fuel and Low-Emission Aviation Technology
nodes.description: Rescinds all unobligated balances from IRA-funded alternative aviation fuel and low-emission aviation technology programs. Bill text: 'Out of the amounts made available by section 40007(a) of title IV of Public Law 117-169 (49 U.S.C. 44504 note), any unobligated balances of such amounts are hereby rescinded.' IRA P.L. 117-169 sec 40007(a) provided approximately $297 million for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) and low-emission aircraft technology development. Rescinded amount = all unobligated balances at enactment. Effective immediately. Contrast: $12.5 billion FAA ATC modernization (SEC. 40003) — large infrastructure investment paired with elimination of clean aviation technology funding.

nodes.title: SEC. 82003 — Loan Rehabilitation: Two-Strike Allowance, $10/mo Minimum
nodes.description: Amends HEA §428F(a)(5) (20 U.S.C. 1078-6(a)(5)) by striking 'one time' and inserting 'two times' — allowing defaulted borrowers to rehabilitate loans twice (previously only once). Also amends §464(h)(1)(D) for Perkins loans similarly. For loans made on/after July 1, 2027: 'the total monthly payment of the borrower for all such loans shall not be less than $10' during rehabilitation. Effective July 1, 2027.

nodes.title: SEC. 70308 — Enhancement of Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit
nodes.description: Increases the §48D advanced manufacturing investment tax credit (CHIPS Act semiconductor manufacturing credit) from 25 percent to 35 percent of qualified investment. §48D(a): '25 percent' replaced with '35 percent'. Combined with §70307 (100% factory building expensing), U.S. semiconductor fab construction could receive combined federal subsidy exceeding 100% of total construction cost in present-value terms. Benefits: TSMC, Intel, Samsung, Micron and other fab manufacturers. Effective: property placed in service after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70510 — Modifications of Zero-Emission Nuclear Power Production Credit
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 45U(c) by adding new paragraph (3): 'RESTRICTIONS RELATING TO PROHIBITED FOREIGN ENTITIES.' Tier 1 — Specified foreign entities: '(A) IN GENERAL.—No credit shall be determined under subsection (a) for any taxable year beginning after the date of enactment of this paragraph if the taxpayer is a specified foreign entity (as defined in section 7701(a)(51)(B)).' Tier 2 — Foreign-influenced entities: '(B) OTHER PROHIBITED FOREIGN ENTITIES.—No credit shall be determined under subsection (a) for any taxable year beginning after the date which is 2 years after the date of enactment of this paragraph if the taxpayer is a foreign-influenced entity (as defined in section 7701(a)(51)(D), without regard to clause (i)(II) thereof).' Nuclear credit NOT terminated — nuclear is treated favorably throughout Chapter 5. Only foreign-entity restrictions added. Enacted by IRA 2022 § 13101. Benefits: domestic nuclear operators (Constellation Energy, Exelon, Duke, NextEra, SMR developers). Two-year grace period for foreign-influenced entities gives existing JVs time to restructure.

nodes.title: SEC. 100006 — TEMPORARY PROTECTED STATUS FEE (amendment to INA § 244(c)(1)(B), 8 U.S.C. 1254a(c)(1)(B))
nodes.description: Raises TPS application fee ceiling 10-fold from $50 to $500. Amendment text (lines 17094-17126) strikes '$50' and inserts '$500, subject to the adjustments required under clause (ii).' New clause (iii): 'All of the fees collected pursuant to this subparagraph shall be deposited into the general fund of the Treasury.' New clause (iv): 'Fees required to be paid under this subparagraph shall not be waived or reduced.' Prior: fee ceiling $50 with waiver discretion. New: $500 floor (Secretary may set higher), CPI-indexed annually, 100% to Treasury, NO FEE WAIVER. Combined TPS annual cost: $500 re-registration + $550 initial EAD (§ 100003(c)) + $275 annual EAD renewal (§ 100012) = $775-$1,325+/year minimum in government fees. EAD validity capped at 1 year. Effective FY2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 20010 — Enhancement of DoD Resources for Improving Readiness
nodes.description: Appropriates approximately $15.8 billion across 23 line items for across-the-board military readiness improvements. Bill text (lines 3033-3081): 'In addition to amounts otherwise available, there are appropriated to the Secretary of Defense for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029.' Key items: $2,500,000,000 for Air Force facilities sustainment/restoration/modernization; $2,118,000,000 for spares and repairs to keep Air Force aircraft mission capable; $2,000,000,000 for Navy depot and shipyard modernization; $1,640,000,000 for Special Operations Command equipment, readiness, and operations; $1,500,000,000 for Army depot modernization; $1,500,000,000 for increased depot maintenance and shipyard maintenance; $1,400,000,000 'for a pilot program on OPN-8 maritime spares and repair rotable pool'; $700,000,000 'for a pilot program on OPN-8 maritime spares and repair rotable pool for amphibious ships' (both pilot programs lack statutory evaluation framework — unusual for $2.1B combined); $500,000,000 for National Guard unit readiness; $400,000,000 for Marine Corps readiness; $320,000,000 for Joint Special Operations Command; $92,500,000 for completion of Robotic Combat Vehicle prototyping. All funds through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 71109 — Alien Medicaid Eligibility Restriction
nodes.description: Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v) by adding new paragraph (5). 'Notwithstanding the preceding paragraphs of this subsection, beginning on October 1, 2026, except as provided in paragraphs (2) and (4), in no event shall payment be made to a State under this section for medical assistance furnished to an individual unless such individual is — (A) a resident of 1 of the 50 States, the District of Columbia, or a territory of the United States; and (B) either — (i) a citizen or national of the United States; (ii) an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence as an immigrant as defined by sections 101(a)(15) and 101(a)(20) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, excluding, among others, alien visitors, tourists, diplomats, and students who enter the United States temporarily with no intention of abandoning their residence in a foreign country; (iii) an alien who has been granted the status of Cuban and Haitian entrant, as defined in section 501(e) of the Refugee Education Assistance Act of 1980 (Public Law 96-422); or (iv) an individual who lawfully resides in the United States in accordance with a Compact of Free Association referred to in section 402(b)(2)(G) of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996.' Also amends CHIP via 42 U.S.C. 1397gg(e)(1) — except for emergency services under §2105(a)(1)(D)(ii). Excluded: DACA recipients (~580K), TPS holders, parolees (Ukrainian/Afghan humanitarian parole), pending asylum seekers, T-visa trafficking victims, Special Immigrant Visa holders before LPR adjustment, lawfully present non-immigrants on work/student visas. Emergency Medicaid (paragraph 2) and pregnant women/children state option (paragraph 4) preserved. ,000,000 appropriated FY2026. Effective October 1, 2026. Estimated 1.5–2 million non-citizen non-LPR immigrants lose federally matched coverage. California alone covers ~500,000 via expanded Medi-Cal.

nodes.title: SEC. 60016 — Rescission of Funding for Environmental and Climate Justice Block Grants
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 138 of the Clean Air Act (42 U.S.C. 7438) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for the Environmental and Climate Justice Block Grant program under CAA Sec. 138 (42 U.S.C. 7438), which provided grants to community-based organizations in disadvantaged communities for pollution monitoring, mitigation, and resilience projects. IRA appropriated $3 billion under Sec. 60201. Program statute is NOT repealed. PATTERN: Combined with Sec. 60001 and Sec. 60002, this represents a concentrated elimination of programs disproportionately targeted at low-income and minority communities. Effective on enactment. Losers: environmental justice organizations, frontline communities near industrial facilities, tribal and rural low-income communities.

nodes.title: SEC. 71305 — Eliminating Limitation on Recapture of Advance Payment of Premium Tax Credit
nodes.description: Section 36B(f)(2) is amended by striking subparagraph (B) — the subparagraph that contained income-graduated repayment caps. CONFORMING AMENDMENTS: (1) Section 36B(f)(2) is amended by striking 'ADVANCE PAYMENTS.—' and all that follows through 'If the advance payments' and inserting: 'ADVANCE PAYMENTS.—If the advance payments'. (2) Section 35(g)(12)(B)(ii) is amended by striking 'then section 36B(f)(2)(B) shall be applied by substituting the amount determined under clause (i) for the amount determined under section 36B(f)(2)(A)' and inserting 'then the amount determined under clause (i) shall be substituted for the amount determined under section 36B(f)(2)'. EFFECTIVE DATE: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025. [Lines 14544–14562]

nodes.title: Cross-title financial regulator independence reduction: Title III CFPB and SEC changes fit a pattern of reducing agency autonomy
nodes.description: Title III contains two provisions that directly reduce the operational independence of major financial regulators: (1) SEC. 30001 cuts the CFPB funding cap from 12% to 6.5% of Federal Reserve operating expenses (12 U.S.C. 5497(a)(2)(A)(iii)), bypassing the normal appropriations process and permanently constraining the bureau below ~M/yr; (2) SEC. 30003 eliminates the SEC's M off-budget Reserve Fund (striking 15 U.S.C. 78d(i)), transferring all balances to Treasury on October 1, 2025 and forcing all SEC spending into the standard appropriations process. Analysis: 'Both agencies are now more dependent on annual appropriations processes or statutory caps set by Congress, reducing their ability to act without legislative approval.' This pattern — moving independent agencies toward greater congressional budget control — is structural and differs from the IRA rescission pattern in mechanism (statutory cap amendment and fund elimination vs. unobligated balance rescission) but shares a common goal of reducing executive/independent agency autonomy. Neither change is indexed to inflation or subject to any waiver authority.

nodes.title: SEC. 50304 — Rescission of NPS and BLM Funds
nodes.description: 'There are rescinded the unobligated balances of amounts made available by the following sections of Public Law 117–169 (commonly known as the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022) (136 Stat. 1818): (1) Section 50221 (136 Stat. 2052). (2) Section 50222 (136 Stat. 2052). (3) Section 50223 (136 Stat. 2052).' Straight rescission of unobligated IRA appropriations for NPS and BLM administrative and conservation programs. Amount indeterminate (depends on remaining unobligated balances) but IRA had appropriated hundreds of millions for NPS/BLM operations, conservation, and deferred maintenance. Irony: immediately follows SEC. 50303 (builds new revenue framework) and immediately precedes SEC. 50305 (M 250th anniversary spectacle) — NPS operating funds cut while event money added. Effective immediately on enactment.

nodes.title: SEC. 10303 — Producer Election
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 9015 and 7 USC 1508(c)(4)(C)(iv). Extends PLC/ARC program election cycle through 2031. Adds 2026 as additional election year. Critical new provision at subsection (i): 'HIGHER OF PRICE LOSS COVERAGE PAYMENTS AND AGRICULTURE RISK COVERAGE PAYMENTS.—For the 2025 crop year, the Secretary shall, on a covered commodity-by-covered commodity basis, make the higher of price loss coverage payments under section 1116 and agriculture risk coverage county coverage payments under section 1117 to the producers on a farm for the payment acres for each covered commodity on the farm.' Also: 2027-2031 crop years are locked to same coverage as 2025 choice. Federal Crop Insurance SCO amendment: strikes 'Crops for which the producer has elected under section 1116 of the Agricultural Act of 2014 to receive agriculture risk coverage and acres' and inserts 'Acres' — removes restriction that blocked SCO for ARC-enrolled acres, making SCO available to all enrolled acres regardless of program choice.

nodes.title: Integrated Enforcement Pipeline — $120B border enforcement architecture
nodes.description: Sections 90001–90004 and 90007 function as an integrated enforcement architecture: Sec. 90001 ($46.55B) builds physical barriers including primary, waterborne, and secondary barriers plus 'any work necessary to prepare the ground'; Sec. 90002 ($12B) expands CBP workforce with 'rehired annuitants' bypassing OPM civil service competition rules; Sec. 90003 ($45B) detains 'until such aliens are removed' — indefinite detention by statute; Sec. 90004 ($6.168B) adds AI/ML/autonomous surveillance; Sec. 90007 ($10B) is an unconstrained Secretary-level catch-all. Combined: approximately $120 billion in a single enforcement cycle — a generational investment in enforcement infrastructure, dwarfing all prior border security appropriations combined.

nodes.title: SEC. 82004 — Public Service Loan Forgiveness: RAP Payments Qualify
nodes.description: Amends HEA §455(m)(1)(A) (20 U.S.C. 1087e(m)(1)(A)) by adding new clause (v): 'on-time payments under the Repayment Assistance Plan under subsection (q)' as qualifying PSLF payments. Preserves continuity for public servants transitioned from ICR/SAVE plans to RAP — they do not lose credit toward 10-year PSLF forgiveness. Borrowers working in qualifying public service jobs making RAP payments continue to accrue PSLF qualifying payment months.

nodes.title: SEC. 70309 — Spaceports Are Treated Like Airports Under Exempt Facility Bond Rules
nodes.description: Amends §142(a)(1): 'airports' to 'airports and spaceports' — allows tax-exempt private activity bonds for spaceport facilities. New §142(p): spaceport = facility at/near launch or reentry site for (A) manufacturing/assembling/repairing spacecraft/space cargo; (B) flight control operations; (C) launch/reentry services; (D) crew/participant/cargo transfer. 'Space cargo' includes satellites, scientific experiments, payloads. 'Spacecraft' = launch or reentry vehicle. Public use requirement does NOT apply to spaceports (unlike airports). Manufacturing facilities and industrial parks at spaceports explicitly allowed (§142(c)(2)(E) inapplicable). Ground leases from U.S. government don't disqualify. §149(b)(3)(F): federal rent/user fees don't make bonds 'federally guaranteed.' Effective: obligations issued after date of enactment. Benefits: SpaceX, Blue Origin, state/local bond issuers for space infrastructure.

nodes.title: SEC. 60017 — Rescission of Funding for ESA Recovery Plans
nodes.description: Verbatim bill text: 'The unobligated balances of amounts made available to carry out section 60301 of Public Law 117-169 (136 Stat. 2079) are rescinded.' Analysis: Cancels unspent IRA funds for Endangered Species Act species recovery plan development and implementation under IRA Sec. 60301. IRA appropriated $125 million. ESA itself (16 U.S.C. 1533) is unaffected. Effective on enactment. Losers: Fish and Wildlife Service and NOAA Fisheries recovery programs; species near delisting thresholds. Beneficiaries: Treasury; development interests in habitat areas.

nodes.title: SEC. 40011 — Rescission of Amounts Appropriated to Public Wireless Supply Chain Innovation Fund
nodes.description: Permanently rescinds $850,000,000 from unobligated balances of the CHIPS Act Public Wireless Supply Chain Innovation Fund. Bill text: 'Of the unobligated balances of amounts made available under section 106(a) of the CHIPS Act of 2022 (Public Law 117-167; 136 Stat. 1392), $850,000,000 are permanently rescinded.' Fund was established under CHIPS Act with ~$1.5 billion to support Open RAN (open, interoperable 5G networks) and reduce telecom dependence on Chinese vendors (Huawei, ZTE). 'Permanently rescinded' — stronger than ordinary rescission; cannot be restored without new legislation. Eliminates more than half of remaining unobligated fund balance. Harmed: Open RAN ecosystem (Mavenir, Parallel Wireless, Altiostar/Fujitsu, Rakuten Symphony); rural carriers seeking Huawei/ZTE rip-and-replace alternatives. Internal tension: SEC. 40002 expands spectrum auction for 5G deployment while SEC. 40011 defunds the trusted-vendor supply chain those deployments require.

nodes.title: SEC. 71110 — Expansion FMAP for Emergency Medicaid (FMAP Reduction)
nodes.description: Amends 42 U.S.C. 1396d by adding new subsection (kk). 'FMAP FOR TREATMENT OF AN EMERGENCY MEDICAL CONDITION.—Notwithstanding subsection (y) and (z), beginning on October 1, 2026, the Federal medical assistance percentage for payments for care and services described in paragraph (2) of subsection 1903(v) furnished to an alien described in paragraph (1) of such subsection shall not exceed the Federal medical assistance percentage determined under subsection (b) for such State.' Effect: expansion states currently use 90% expansion FMAP (§1905(y) and (z)) for emergency Medicaid for undocumented immigrants. This section caps FMAP at regular state-specific rate (typically 50–77%). California FMAP ~50% — federal cost share drops from 90% to 50% for emergency alien Medicaid. Note: title 'Expansion FMAP' is misleading — it REDUCES FMAP, does not expand it. Section title refers to expansion states, not benefit expansion. ,000,000 FY2026 implementation. Effective October 1, 2026.

nodes.title: SEC. 50305 — Celebrating America's 250th Anniversary
nodes.description: 'there is appropriated to the Secretary of the Interior (acting through the Director of the National Park Service) for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, ,000,000 for events, celebrations, and activities surrounding the observance and commemoration of the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States, to remain available through fiscal year 2028.' Standalone appropriation of ,000,000. Ironic placement: directly after rescission of NPS operating funds in §50304. NPS operational capacity cut while M allocated for commemorative spectacle. Benefits tourism and hospitality sector. No organic connection to energy policy — anomalous provision in Energy and Natural Resources title. Available FY2025-2028.

nodes.title: Family Detention — Flores Settlement Workaround via Statute
nodes.description: Sec. 90003(b)-(c) authorizes detention of families including accompanied children 'pending a decision on whether the aliens are to be removed from the United States and, if such aliens are ordered removed from the United States, until such aliens are removed.' The definition of 'family residential center' explicitly includes 'alien children who are not unaccompanied alien children (as defined in section 462(g) of the Homeland Security Act of 2002 (6 U.S.C. 279(g)))' — i.e., accompanied children. The Flores settlement agreement (Flores v. Reno, C.D. Cal. 1997) and Ninth Circuit rulings have historically limited family detention. This provision is structured to provide statutory authority the government will argue supersedes Flores's consent decree limitations — though the statute does not mention Flores by name. Detention standards for single adults set 'in the discretion of the Secretary of Homeland Security' — effectively overriding ICE Performance-Based National Detention Standards.

nodes.title: SEC. 100007 — VISA INTEGRITY FEE (8 U.S.C. 1806)
nodes.description: New $250 fee on every alien issued a nonimmigrant visa (B-1/B-2, F-1, J-1, H-1B, O-1, etc.). Verbatim (lines 17128-17174): 'the Secretary of Homeland Security shall require the payment of a fee, equal to the amount specified in this subsection, by any alien issued a nonimmigrant visa at the time of such issuance.' INITIAL: greater of $250 or higher by rule. CPI-indexed rounded down to nearest dollar (not $10). DISPOSITION: 'All of the fees collected pursuant to this section that are not reimbursed pursuant to subsection (b) shall be deposited into the general fund of the Treasury.' REIMBURSEMENT (§ 100007(b)): Secretary 'may provide a reimbursement' if alien demonstrates: (1) 'complied with all conditions of such nonimmigrant visa, including the condition that an alien shall not accept unauthorized employment'; AND (2)(A) 'has not sought to extend his or her period of admission during such period of validity and departed the United States not later than 5 days after the last day of such period' OR (2)(B) was granted extension or adjustment to LPR status. Fee is imposed at issuance; reimbursement is discretionary, requires active application. Affects millions of annual visitors from all countries. No fee waiver. Cross-refs: INA § 217 (VWP), INA § 281, existing visa fee schedules.

nodes.title: SEC. 10304 — Price Loss Coverage
nodes.description: Amends 7 USC 9016. Extends PLC payment authority through 2031 (from 2023/2025). Subsection (a)(2): strikes '2023' and inserts '2031'. Subsection (c)(1)(B): extends through 2031. Subsection (d): strikes '2025' and inserts '2031'. Rice benchmark update in subsection (g): strikes '2012 through 2016' and inserts '2017 through 2021' for long grain rice historical price benchmark — uses higher-priced period, which will reduce PLC payments to rice farmers when market prices exceed old but not new benchmark. No new dollar amounts; cost flows from higher reference prices (SEC. 10301) and expanded base acres (SEC. 10302).

nodes.title: SEC. 71303 + 71305 interaction: Retroactive verification failures generate uncapped APTC repayment liability — potential for catastrophic tax bills on good-faith enrollees
nodes.description: Verification failures under SEC. 71303 that retroactively disqualify months as 'coverage months' will generate overpayments. Those overpayments are now fully collectable under SEC. 71305 with no income-based cap. A person who enrolled in good faith may face full repayment of an entire year's worth of advance premium tax credits if a retroactive verification failure is discovered. Previously, a family at 200% FPL might owe a maximum of ~,500; they will now owe the full excess, which could be thousands of dollars. Creates severe 'benefits cliff' and income volatility risk for gig workers, seasonal workers, part-time workers, self-employed individuals.

nodes.title: SEC. 20011 — Improving DoD Border Support and Counter-Drug Missions
nodes.description: Appropriates $1,000,000,000 to the Secretary of Defense for military border operations and — critically — migrant detention on military installations. Bill text (lines 3084-3094), verbatim: 'there are appropriated to the Secretary of Defense for fiscal year 2025, out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated, to remain available until September 30, 2029, $1,000,000,000 for the deployment of military personnel in support of border operations, operations and maintenance activities in support of border operations, counter-narcotics and counter-transnational criminal organization mission support, the operation of national defense areas and construction in national defense areas, and the temporary detention of migrants on Department of Defense installations, in accordance with chapter 15 of title 10, United States Code.' Five activities funded in a single lump sum: (1) military personnel deployment at border; (2) O&M costs for border operations; (3) counter-narcotics/counter-TCO missions (traditional under 10 U.S.C. § 284); (4) operation/construction of national defense areas (post-2025 border militarization policy converting border land to national defense areas, removing civilian law enforcement primacy); (5) 'temporary detention of migrants on Department of Defense installations' — immigration detention by military, not DHS. Chapter 15 citation invokes Insurrection Act/military support to law enforcement authority. No specified legal framework for detainee rights or oversight. This section embeds immigration enforcement within defense appropriations, outside DHS oversight structures and ICE detention standards. Funds through September 30, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 70311 — Modifications Related to Foreign Tax Credit Limitation
nodes.description: Changes deduction allocation rules for the FTC limitation when computing the net CFC tested income (formerly GILTI) basket. New §904(b)(5): for amounts in §904(d)(1)(A) (GILTI/net CFC tested income basket), foreign-source taxable income is computed by: (A) allocating §250(a)(1)(B) deduction AND §164(a)(3) state taxes on those amounts TO the GILTI basket; (B) allocating ZERO interest expense or R&D expenditures to GILTI basket (allocated entirely to U.S. basket instead); (C) allocating other deductions to GILTI only if directly traceable. Net effect: maximizes foreign-source income in GILTI basket, maximizes FTC utilization, reduces effective GILTI rate for companies with large interest/R&D. §904(d)(2)(H)(i): updated cross-reference. §904(d)(4)(C)(ii): updated cross-reference. §951A(f)(1)(A): updated cross-reference. Effective: tax years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 82005 — Student Loan Servicing: $1 Billion Mandatory Appropriation
