SEPTEMBER 30, 2028:
  - SNAP work requirement sunset for noncontiguous states only (node 20 — contiguous states permanent).

SEPTEMBER 30, 2029:
  - SEC. 71116: State directed payment cap tightens (transitional glide path ends).

SEPTEMBER 30, 2034:
  - SEC. 35: MSP enrollment streamlining moratorium expires (node 35).
  - SEC. 51: Medicaid/CHIP/BHP enrollment streamlining moratorium expires (node 51).
  - SEC. 60012: Methane fee compliance period extension expires — fee enforcement resumes (node 111).
  - SEC. 71111: Nursing home staffing moratorium expires (node 170).

INDEFINITE / NO SUNSET:
  - Title VII TCJA permanent extensions (individual rates, CTC, estate tax exemption, etc.).
  - Title IX border wall construction (node 43) — ongoing appropriation.
  - SEC. 72001: $5T debt ceiling increase (node 230) — statutory until debt approaches limit.
  - SEC. 71401: Rural Health Transformation Program (FY2026-FY2030, node 209).

nodes.title: SEC. 70106 — Extension and Enhancement of Increased Estate and Gift Tax Exemption Amounts
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 2010(c)(3)(A) to replace '$5,000,000' with '$15,000,000' as the base exemption amount. Updates inflation base year from 2011 to 2026 and base calendar year from 2010 to 2025. Deletes § 2010(c)(3)(C) (the TCJA sunset provision). Result: per-person exemption is ~$15M+ inflation-adjusted from 2026; married couples ~$30M+ combined via portability. Applies to estates of decedents dying and gifts made after December 31, 2025. Revenue impact: eliminates estate tax for virtually all but ultra-high-net-worth estates (pre-TCJA ~5,500 estates/year; TCJA ~2,000/year; this further narrows to fewer).

nodes.title: SEC. 70107 — Extension of Increased AMT Exemption Amounts and Modification of Phase-Out Thresholds
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 55(d)(4) to permanently extend TCJA higher AMT exemptions (removes 'and before January 1, 2026'). Modifies inflation adjustment: base year 2018 for $109,400 and $70,300 amounts; base year 2025 for the $1,000,000 phase-out threshold. STEEPENS phase-out rate from 25% to 50% for income above the $1,000,000 threshold (adds new subclause (IV) substituting '50 percent' for '25 percent'). Effect: AMT exemptions remain high (protecting ~5M taxpayers who previously paid AMT pre-TCJA), but the phase-out is faster for ultra-high earners. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70108 — Extension and Modification of Limitation on Deduction for Qualified Residence Interest
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 163(h)(3)(F) to permanently extend TCJA's $750,000 mortgage debt cap (removes 'and before January 1, 2026'). Retitles from '2018 THROUGH 2025' to 'BEGINNING AFTER 2017'. Adds new subclause (III): 'MORTGAGE INSURANCE PREMIUMS TREATED AS INTEREST — Clause (iv) of subparagraph (E) shall not apply.' — this permanently restores deductibility of mortgage insurance premiums by deleting the exclusion clause (ii) and renumbering remaining clauses. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70109 — Extension and Modification of Limitation on Casualty Loss Deduction
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 165(h)(5)(A) to permanently extend TCJA casualty loss restriction (only federally declared disasters deductible). Extends coverage to 'State declared disaster' — defined as natural catastrophe (hurricane, tornado, storm, high water, wind-driven water, tidal wave, tsunami, earthquake, volcanic eruption, landslide, mudslide, snowstorm, drought) or fire, flood, or explosion that the Governor (or DC Mayor) AND the Secretary of Treasury jointly determine causes damage of sufficient severity. 'State' includes DC, Puerto Rico, Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, Northern Mariana Islands. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70110 — Termination of Miscellaneous Itemized Deductions Other Than Educator Expenses
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 67(g) to permanently eliminate 2%-of-AGI-floor miscellaneous itemized deductions (removes sunset). Creates educator expenses exception in § 67(b)(13): deductions under § 162 for 'educator expenses' are not subject to the floor. New § 67(g) defines 'educator expenses' more broadly than § 62(a)(2)(D): (1) applies without the $300 dollar limitation, (2) without the exclusion of 'nonathletic supplies for courses of instruction in health or physical education,' and (3) substituting 'as part of instructional activity' for 'in the classroom.' Also expands educator definition to include 'interscholastic sports administrator or coach' (via § 62(d)(1)(A) modification). Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70111 — Limitation on Tax Benefit of Itemized Deductions (Pease Restoration)
nodes.description: Completely rewrites IRC § 68. New rule: itemized deductions for any individual are reduced by 2/37 of the LESSER of (1) total itemized deductions, or (2) so much of taxable income (computed without this section, increased by itemized deductions) as exceeds the dollar amount at which the 37% rate bracket begins. Applied AFTER all other limitations (§ 68(b)). QBI explicitly carved out: § 199A(e)(1) amended to compute taxable income 'without regard to section 68'; § 199A(g)(2)(B) amended 'without regard to section 68 or.' Effect: caps the tax-rate benefit of itemized deductions at 35% for 37%-bracket taxpayers (37% × (1 - 2/37) = 35%). Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70112 — Extension and Modification of Qualified Transportation Fringe Benefits
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 132(f) to permanently eliminate qualified bicycle commuting reimbursement from tax-free fringe benefits: strikes subparagraph (D) of § 132(f)(1); strikes subparagraph (C) of § 132(f)(2); strikes '(other than a qualified bicycle commuting reimbursement)' in § 132(f)(4); strikes subparagraph (F) of § 132(f)(5); strikes § 132(f)(8). Inflation adjustment: changes base year from 1998 to 1997 in § 132(f)(6)(A)(ii). § 274(l) amended to remove bicycle commuting employer deduction rules. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70113 — Extension and Modification of Limitation on Deduction and Exclusion for Moving Expenses
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 217(k) to permanently extend TCJA suspension of civilian moving expense deduction (removes sunset). Adds § 217(k)(2): employees/new appointees of the intelligence community (as defined in § 3 of the National Security Act of 1947, 50 U.S.C. 3003) who move pursuant to a change in assignment requiring relocation are treated the same as armed forces personnel under § 217(g) — deduction allowed. Same treatment for employer exclusion in § 132(g)(2). The intelligence community definition covers 18 agencies (CIA, NSA, DIA, etc.). Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70114 — Extension and Modification of Limitation on Wagering Losses
nodes.description: Completely rewrites IRC § 165(d). New rule: losses from wagering transactions are (A) limited to 90% of such losses (not 100%), AND (B) allowed only to the extent of gains from wagering transactions during the year. 'Losses from wagering transactions' defined to include ALL deductions otherwise allowable under chapter 1 incurred in carrying on any wagering transaction — explicitly capturing professional gamblers' business expenses (travel, subscriptions, etc.). This is a permanent 10% haircut on gambling losses and a permanent gains-only limitation. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70115 — Extension and Enhancement of Increased Limitation on Contributions to ABLE Accounts
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 529A(b)(2)(B) to permanently extend higher ABLE account contribution limits (removes 'before January 1, 2026' from clause (ii)). Also adjusts inflation calculation: inserts '(determined by substituting 1996 for 1997 in paragraph (2)(B) thereof)' after 'section 2503(b)' in clause (i), updating the base year for the annual gift tax exclusion amount that caps standard ABLE contributions. Benefits employed individuals with disabilities whose disability arose before age 26. Effective: contributions made after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70116 — Extension and Enhancement of Saver's Credit Allowed for ABLE Contributions
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 25B to: (1) Extend Saver's Credit eligibility for ABLE account contributions: rewrites § 25B(d)(1) to define 'qualified retirement savings contributions' to include ABLE contributions AND (for taxable years beginning before January 1, 2027) standard retirement contributions (elective deferrals, IRA contributions, voluntary employee contributions). (2) REPEALS § 103(e)(1) of the SECURE 2.0 Act of 2022 — the provision that would have converted the Saver's Credit into a direct 'Saver's Match' paid to retirement accounts for low-income workers starting 2027. IRC applied as if that section never enacted. (3) Raises Saver's Credit max from $2,000 to $2,100 starting taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026. SECURE 2.0 repeal effective taxable years ending after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70117 — Extension of Rollovers from Qualified Tuition Programs to ABLE Accounts
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 529(c)(3)(C)(i)(III) by striking 'before January 1, 2026' — permanently allows rollover of unused 529 college savings plan funds into an ABLE account for the same beneficiary or a family member with a disability. No dollar cap is specified; general ABLE contribution limits apply. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70118 — Extension of Treatment of Sinai Peninsula; Enhancement to Include Additional Hazardous Duty Areas
nodes.description: Amends § 11026(a) of P.L. 115-97 (TCJA) to permanently extend combat-zone tax exclusion for Sinai Peninsula by removing 'with respect to the applicable period.' Rewrites § 11026(b) to define 'qualified hazardous duty area' as: (1) the Sinai Peninsula of Egypt, (2) Kenya, (3) Mali, (4) Burkina Faso, (5) Chad — but ONLY during the period for which any member of the Armed Forces is entitled to special pay under 37 U.S.C. § 310 (hostile fire or imminent danger pay) for services in such location. Deletes former subsections (c) and (d). Effective: January 1, 2026. Reflects U.S. counterterrorism operations in the Sahel without formal combat zone designation.

nodes.title: SEC. 70119 — Extension and Modification of Exclusion from Gross Income of Student Loans Discharged on Account of Death or Disability
nodes.description: Rewrites IRC § 108(f)(5) to permanently extend (removes TCJA sunset) and expand discharge-of-student-loan income exclusion. Covers discharges: (i) pursuant to § 437(a) or (d) of the Higher Education Act (federal loan repayment/death/disability provisions) or Part D equivalent, (ii) pursuant to HEA § 464(c)(1)(F), or (iii) otherwise discharged on account of death or total and permanent disability. NEW: extends to private education loans (as defined in § 140(a) of the Consumer Credit Protection Act, 15 U.S.C. 1650(a)) — previously only federal loans covered. SSN requirement added: § 24(h)(7) standard applies; omission treated as mathematical/clerical error under § 6213(g)(2)(X). Effective: discharges after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SEC. 70120 — Limitation on Individual Deductions for Certain State and Local Taxes (SALT Cap)
nodes.description: Amends IRC § 164(b)(6) to replace flat $10,000 cap with 'applicable limitation amount' (half for MFS). New § 164(b)(7) defines applicable limitation amount: 2025 = $40,000; 2026 = $40,400; 2027-2029 = 101% of prior year (~$40,804 / $41,212 / $41,624); 2030+ = $10,000 (hard reversion). Phase-down: for MAGI above threshold (2025 = $500,000; 2026 = $505,000; 2027+ = 101% compounding), cap reduced by 30% of excess MAGI, but NOT below $10,000. Break-even: at $533,333 MAGI (2025), 30% × $33,333 = $10,000 reduction — cap fully phased to $10,000. MAGI = AGI + § 911, 931, 933 exclusions. MFS gets half the threshold. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024 (retroactive to TY 2025). Hard reversion for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 70201 — No Tax on Tips (New IRC § 224)
nodes.description: Creates new IRC § 224 'Qualified Tips' — above-the-line deduction (added to § 63(b)(5)) equal to qualified tips reported on W-2 box 18, Form 4137, or via §§ 6041(d)(3), 6041A(e)(3), 6050W(f)(2). Cap: $25,000/year. Phase-out: reduced by $100 per $1,000 of MAGI above $150,000 ($300,000 joint); full phase-out at ~$400,000/$600,000. 'Qualified tips' = cash tips (including charged tips and tip-sharing) in occupations that 'customarily and regularly received tips on or before December 31, 2024' per Secretary's list. EXCLUSIONS: (A) must be voluntary, not subject to negotiation, determined by payor; (B) employer trade/business is NOT a specified service trade or business (§ 199A(d)(2)) — employee tainted by employer's SSTB status; (C) Secretary may add requirements. Tip income excluded from QBI (§ 199A(c)(4)(D)). FICA tip credit § 45B extended to beauty services (barbering, hair care, nail care, esthetics, body/spa). W-2 box 18 reporting required; W-4 withholding adjustment by Jan 1, 2026. Treasury must publish qualifying occupation list within 90 days of enactment. SSN required (§ 24(h)(7) standard). Joint return required for married filers. Tips remain subject to FICA. Expires: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.

nodes.title: SEC. 70202 — No Tax on Overtime (New IRC § 225)
nodes.description: Creates new IRC § 225 'Qualified Overtime Compensation' — above-the-line deduction (added to § 63(b)(6)) equal to qualified overtime compensation included on W-2 box 19 or §§ 6041(d)(4), 6051(a)(19). Cap: $12,500 ($25,000 joint). Phase-out: reduced by $100 per $1,000 of MAGI above $150,000 ($300,000 joint) — same as tips deduction. 'Qualified overtime compensation' = overtime pay required under FLSA § 7 (29 U.S.C. 207) that is IN EXCESS of the regular rate — i.e., ONLY the premium 'half' of time-and-a-half, NOT the full overtime pay. Example: $20/hr regular, 10 hrs OT = $100 deductible (the extra $10/hr × 10 hrs), not $300 total. Qualified tips explicitly excluded from overtime definition. FLSA-exempt workers (salaried managers, professionals) excluded. W-2 box 19 reporting required; withholding adjustment by Jan 1, 2026. SSN required (§ 24(h)(7)). Joint return required for married. FICA taxes still apply. Expires: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2028. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2024.

nodes.title: SEC. 70203 — No Tax on Car Loan Interest (Qualified Passenger Vehicle Loan Interest Deduction)
nodes.description: Adds new IRC § 163(h)(4) (renumbers prior (4) to (5)) excluding 'qualified passenger vehicle loan interest' from 'personal interest' (normally nondeductible). Deduction added to § 63(b)(7). 'Qualified passenger vehicle loan interest' = interest paid or accrued on indebtedness incurred after December 31, 2024, secured by FIRST LIEN on an 'applicable passenger vehicle' for personal use. EXCLUDED: fleet loans, commercial vehicle loans, lease financing, salvage title loans, scrap/parts vehicles. VIN must be reported on return. Dollar cap: $10,000/year. Phase-out: reduced by $200 per $1,000 of MAGI above $100,000 ($200,000 joint) — full phase-out at $150,000/$250,000 MAGI (steep 20% rate). 'Applicable passenger vehicle': new (original use commences with taxpayer), public street vehicle, 2+ wheels, car/minivan/van/SUV/pickup/motorcycle, Clean Air Act motor vehicle, GVWR < 14,000 lbs, AND final assembly in the United States. 'Final assembly' = manufacturer produces vehicle at a plant with all component parts necessary for mechanical operation. Refinancing permitted up to original balance. Related-party loans excluded. New § 6050AA requires lenders receiving $600+ in interest to file Form 1098-type information returns. AMT conforming amendment: § 56(e)(1)(B). Effective: indebtedness incurred after December 31, 2024. Expires: January 1, 2029.

nodes.title: SEC. 70204 — Trump Accounts and Contribution Pilot Program (New IRC §§ 530A, 128, 139J, 6434, 6659)
nodes.description: Creates new children's savings system with multiple IRC provisions: IRC § 530A (Trump Accounts): Non-Roth traditional IRA for individuals under 18. Locked until beneficiary's 18th birthday. Investments restricted to eligible investments: mutual fund or ETF that tracks a qualified index (S&P 500 or other broad US equity index with regulated futures traded on qualified exchange), no leverage, fees ≤ 0.1%, no sector-specific funds. Annual private contribution limit: $5,000 (inflation-indexed from 2026 base). NO deduction allowed for contributions before age 18 (§ 530A(c)(1)). Secretary may auto-create accounts using tax return information (§ 530A(b)(2)(C)(i)). At 18, converts to regular IRA (distributions taxed as ordinary income). Qualified ABLE rollover: at age 17, entire balance can be rolled to ABLE account (§ 530A(d)(4)). Death before 18: account ceases to be Trump Account; FMV minus investment in contract includible in income (§ 530A(d)(6)). Trustee selection criteria: reliability, customer service, costs. Reporting: contributions over $25 from non-Secretary/non-parent must be disclosed (§ 530A(i)(1)(A)). Qualified General Contributions (§ 530A(f)): state/local governments, Indian tribal governments, § 501(c)(3) orgs can make bulk contributions divided equally among defined classes of beneficiaries (all US under-18 accounts; by geography if 5,000+ beneficiaries in area; by birth year). These excluded from income under § 139J. IRC § 128 (Employer Contributions): Employers may contribute up to $2,500/year to Trump Accounts of employees or dependents as tax-free fringe benefit (inflation-indexed from 2026). IRC § 6434 (Pilot Program): $1,000 refundable credit paid directly to Trump Account for each eligible child: born January 1, 2025–December 31, 2028; U.S. citizen; qualifying child per § 152(c); SSN per § 24(h)(7) required before date of election. Protected from federal debt offset (§ 6402). Interest on payments does not begin before January 1, 2028. IRC § 6659 (Penalties): $500 negligence or $1,000 fraud penalty for improper pilot program claim. FUNDING: $410,000,000 appropriated to Treasury, available through September 30, 2034 — covers ~410,000 children of ~14-15 million born 2025-2028. Accounts open 12 months after enactment. Effective: taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025.

nodes.title: SALT Cap vs. State Fiscal Impacts from Medicaid Cuts
nodes.description: SEC. 70120 raises SALT deduction cap to $40,000 (2025–2029) for households with MAGI below $500,000, providing meaningful relief to middle-to-upper-middle income taxpayers in high-tax states (California, New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Illinois). However, the same high-tax states that benefit most from SALT relief face the largest Medicaid fiscal pressure from Title VII-B (node 11) cuts — CBO estimated Medicaid spending reductions force states to choose between maintaining coverage and raising state taxes. The SALT cap relief may be partially or fully offset by increased state income/property taxes imposed to backfill Medicaid shortfalls, particularly in the high-SALT states where the cap increase has the most value. The 2029 hard reversion to $10,000 creates a fiscal cliff coinciding with the period when Medicaid restructuring effects will be most acute at the state level.

nodes.title: Child Tax Credit SSN Restriction: Cross-Title Immigration Nexus
nodes.description: SEC. 70104 rewrites IRC § 24(h)(7)(B) to define 'social security number' as only SSNs issued to U.S. citizens or pursuant to § 205(c)(2)(B)(i) of the Social Security Act (i.e., valid work-authorized immigration status), AND issued before the return due date. This SSN definition is then incorporated by cross-reference into ALL of the following provisions: § 151(d)(5)(C) (senior deduction, § 70103), IRC § 224(e) (tips deduction, § 70201), IRC § 225(d) (overtime deduction, § 70202), IRC § 530A(b)(2)(B) (Trump Accounts eligibility, § 70204), IRC § 6434(e) (pilot program payment, § 70204). Effect: undocumented immigrants and certain lawfully present immigrants without qualifying SSNs are excluded from CTC, senior deduction, tips deduction, overtime deduction, and Trump Accounts simultaneously. This operates in tandem with Title X (node 15) immigration enforcement provisions and Title I (node 2) SNAP eligibility restrictions.

nodes.title: Trump Accounts vs. Student Loan Changes: Competing Savings Incentives
nodes.description: SEC. 70204 creates Trump Accounts (IRC § 530A) — tax-deferred children's savings vehicles with $5,000/year private contribution limit, restricted to US equity index funds, locked until age 18, with a $410M pilot providing ~$1,000 to eligible children born 2025-2028. The accounts are NOT deductible (unlike traditional IRAs) and distributions are taxed as ordinary income — the primary benefit is tax deferral. Title VIII (node 13, Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions) includes student loan provisions that may alter the higher-education financing landscape. Key tension: Trump Accounts encourage wealth-building via equity investing for children, but (1) the $410M appropriation covers fewer than 3% of eligible children, (2) contributions are post-tax with deferred income-tax distributions (less favorable than Roth IRAs for low-income families), and (3) SEC. 70119 (§ 70119) quietly extends tax-free discharge treatment for student loans killed by death/disability — suggesting the bill simultaneously creates new savings incentives while maintaining debt relief for the most severe cases. The competing policy signals (save for education vs. borrow for education) are not harmonized across titles.

nodes.title: Estate Tax Exemption Distributional Impact: Concentrated Benefit at the Very Top
nodes.description: SEC. 70106 raises the estate tax exemption from $5,000,000 base (producing ~$13.6M inflation-adjusted per-person exemption in 2025) to $15,000,000 base (inflation-adjusted from 2026). For a married couple, portability means ~$30M+ combined exemption. At 40% marginal estate tax rate, the incremental benefit relative to pre-bill TCJA levels for an estate exactly at $15M is: the $15M-$13.6M = ~$1.4M gap × 40% = ~$560,000 per person in eliminated estate tax. For an estate of $50M (single person), the tax savings relative to TCJA law is ~($15M - $13.6M) × 40% = ~$560,000 additional savings beyond TCJA. Relative to pre-TCJA law (prior $5.49M exemption, 2017): the full $15M provision saves estates ~$3.8M in tax per person (($15M - $5.49M) × 40%). The CBO/JCT distribution tables consistently show estate tax benefits accrue exclusively to the top 0.1% of decedents. Combined with permanent TCJA rate reductions (§ 70101), permanent AMT relief (§ 70107), and permanent QBI deduction (§ 70105), the Chapter 1 provisions are heavily tilted toward high and very-high income/wealth households, while Chapter 2 provisions (tips, overtime, car loans — all temporary, all expiring 2028) target working-class households. The structural asymmetry — permanent benefits for the wealthy, temporary benefits for workers — is the defining distributional characteristic of Chapters 1 and 2.
